family.intention: We pray that our family may welcome Jesus into our home this week.
family.ask: Ask: “Where shall we keep our blessed palm, and how will we pray together each evening this week?”

illus: An illustration

Every Hosanna Sunday a grandfather in a parish near Thodupuzha sat in the front pew with a bundle of blessed palms on his knees, folding small crosses for every child who came by. He had learnt it from his own grandmother. One year a boy asked him why he took so much trouble over leaves that would dry up in a week. He held up a cross and said: “On Sunday they shout Hosanna. On Friday they shout Crucify. I fold the leaf into a cross so that you will remember both, and stay with him all the way.”

pm.open: Lord Jesus, King of peace, you come to us humble and gentle. We welcome you with our Hosanna. Amen.
share: The scepter shall not depart from Judah (Genesis 49:10). Do I let Jesus truly be the King of my life?
Lo, your king comes to you; triumphant and victorious is he, humble and riding on a donkey (Zechariah 9:9). Where do I need his gentleness rather than force?
It is not you that support the root, but the root that supports you (Romans 11:18). Where has pride crept into my faith?
My house shall be called a house of prayer (Matthew 21:13). What needs to be cleansed in the temple of my heart and my home?
pm.resp: Hosanna! Save us, Lord.
interc: For the Church as she enters the Week of the Passion.
For the Pope, the bishops and all priests who will lead the rites of this holy week.
For peace among nations, through Christ the King of peace.
For the Jewish people, our elder brothers and sisters in faith.
For children, whose praise the Lord loves, and for our families as we follow him this week.
pm.close: Father, your Son entered Jerusalem humble and riding on a donkey, to give his life for us. Make us follow him faithfully this week, from the palms of Hosanna to the Cross and the empty tomb. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: The Passover lamb, whose blood saved Israel, points to Christ, our paschal Lamb.
On the night he was betrayed Jesus said: This is my body; this is my blood of the covenant. He gave us the Holy Qurbana and the priesthood.
The Lord and Teacher washed his disciples' feet: the altar and the basin belong together.
2027-03-25.action: Come to the one Pesaha Qurbana with your whole family, and break the Pesaha appam at home tonight.
2027-03-25.question: Do I receive the Lord's Body with a heart that discerns him and with hands ready to serve?
catechism: The Lord loved his own to the end and instituted the Eucharist.
The Real Presence of Christ in the Eucharist.
The institution of the priesthood at the Last Supper.
kidsaint: St Tarcisius

A boy in Rome about 1,700 years ago who carried the Holy Eucharist to Christians in prison. When some people tried to snatch it from him, he held Jesus close to his heart and would not let go, and he died protecting him. Lesson: Jesus in the Holy Qurbana is our greatest treasure!
2027-03-25.special: Pesaha Thursday: Holy Qurbana of the Lord's Supper, washing of the feet, Pesaha appam and paal at home. The Annunciation is transferred this year.
term: Pesaha
The Syriac form of Pesach, Passover. For the St Thomas Christians it names Holy Thursday, the day of the Lord's Supper, and the Pesaha appam and paal shared by the family that night.

family.explain: On the night before he died, Jesus had a special supper with his friends. He took bread and said: this is my body. He took the cup and said: this is my blood. That is how he gave us the Holy Qurbana. Then he did something surprising: he knelt down and washed his friends' feet, like a servant. He said: I have given you an example; you also should do as I have done. Tonight we break the Pesaha appam together to remember his love.
family.intention: We pray for our priests, for families who cannot be together tonight, and for homes in mourning.
family.ask: Ask: “How can each of us serve someone in our family tonight, as Jesus washed his friends' feet?”

illus: An illustration

In a parish near Kanjirappally, the vicar had a hard year: a senior parishioner had opposed him at every parish council meeting and spoken against him in the town. When the list for the washing of the feet was drawn up, the vicar quietly added that man's name. At the Pesaha Qurbana the old man saw the priest kneel before him with the basin, and his face went red. The priest washed his feet, dried them and kissed them. After the Qurbana the man came to the sacristy, could not say anything, and simply took the priest's hand. That night he sent a piece of his family's Pesaha appam to the parish house.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you loved your own to the end. Be among us now as one who serves, and teach us to love as you have loved. Amen.
share: The blood shall be a sign for you (Exodus 12:13). What does the blood of the Lamb mean for my home and my family?
in every place incense is offered to my name, and a pure offering (Malachi 1:11). Do I bring the Lord my best or what is left over?
This is my body that is for you (1 Corinthians 11:24). How do I prepare to receive the Lord, discerning his Body?
you also ought to wash one another's feet (John 13:14). Whose feet is the Lord asking me to wash?
pm.resp: Lord, you loved us to the end.
interc: For the Church, gathered tonight around one altar in every place.
For our bishops and priests, on the night the Lord instituted the priesthood.
For families who cannot be together tonight, for migrants far from home, and for homes in mourning.
For the sick who receive Holy Communion at home today, and for all who cannot come to the Qurbana.
For the Jewish people, who keep the Passover, and for all who hunger for the Bread of Life.
For our group, that we may serve one another as the Lord served us.
pm.close: Father, on the night before he suffered your Son gave us the sacrament of his Body and Blood and the example of his love. Keep us faithful to his memory, make us one at his altar, and send us out to wash one another's feet. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Abraham was spared his only son; the Father did not spare his.
“By his bruises we are healed”: the Servant bore our sins in silence.
From the Cross: forgiveness, Paradise, a Mother, and “It is finished.”
2027-03-26.action: Forgive one person today, by name, as Jesus forgave from the Cross.
2027-03-26.question: What does the Cross ask of me today, and from whom am I still running?
catechism: God's saving plan in the Passion.
Who is responsible for Christ's death.
kidsaint: The Good Thief

One of the men crucified beside Jesus said, “Jesus, remember me when you come into your kingdom.” Jesus promised him, “Truly I tell you, today you will be with me in Paradise.” (Later tradition calls him Dismas.) Lesson: it is never too late to say sorry to Jesus!
2027-03-26.special: Passion Friday (Good Friday): fasting and abstinence; no Holy Qurbana; service of the Passion, veneration of the Cross, procession, burial of the Cross and kaippuneer.
term: Kaippuneer

The bitter drink given to the faithful at the end of the Passion Friday service in the Syro-Malabar Church. It recalls the sour wine offered to Jesus when he said “I am thirsty” (John 19:28–29), and the bitterness of the Passion that the disciple promises to share.

family.explain: Jesus died on the cross because he loves us. Even on the cross he forgave the people who hurt him, and he promised heaven to the thief who said sorry. He gave his own Mother Mary to be our mother. Today the church has no Qurbana; we kiss the cross and say thank you.
family.intention: We pray for all who are suffering, and we thank Jesus for his love.
family.ask: Ask: “Is there someone I need to forgive today, like Jesus did?”

illus: An illustration

In a house near Pala, a grandfather kept an old wooden crucifix that had belonged to his own father. Every Passion Friday after the church service he placed it on the table, lit a small lamp, and the whole family, from the youngest grandchild to the oldest aunt, came one by one to kiss the feet of the Lord. One year his teenage grandson, home from college in Delhi, hung back. “It is just wood, appacha,” he said. The old man did not argue. He turned the crucifix over and showed him, carved small on the back in his father's hand, the date of the year their family had lost everything in a flood, and the words ‘He did not leave us.’ The boy was silent for a long time. Then he came and knelt.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, crucified for us, we kneel before your Cross. Let us keep watch with you in silence. Amen.
share: Take your son, your only son… whom you love (Genesis 22:2). What did my salvation cost the Father?
He was wounded for our transgressions (Isaiah 53:5). Which of my sins do I see in his wounds?
Father, forgive them (Luke 23:34). Whom do I find it hardest to forgive?
Here is your mother (John 19:27). Have I taken Mary into my home?
It is finished (John 19:30). What must I finally hand over to him today?
pm.resp: Lord, by your holy Cross, have mercy on us.
interc: For the Church throughout the world, that she may be faithful at the foot of the Cross.
For the Jewish people, the first to hear the word of God, that they may grow in love of his name and in faithfulness to his covenant.
For all who suffer: the sick, the persecuted, the lonely, the dying.
For those who have lost faith, that the Cross may speak to them of love.
For our families, that we may forgive one another as Christ forgave.
pm.close: Father, you did not spare your own Son but gave him up for us all. Look on your family gathered at the Cross, and through his blood forgive us, heal us and make us one. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: The Lord rests in the tomb and goes down among the dead to set them free.
Jonah from the belly of the fish: the sign of the Resurrection.
Baptised into his death, we rise to walk in newness of life.
2027-03-27.action: Find the date of your baptism and thank God for it before the Uyirppu.
2027-03-27.question: What in me still needs to be buried with Christ, so that I can rise with him?
catechism: Baptism: burial and rising with Christ.
kidsaint: St Joseph of Arimathea

He was a good and rich man who secretly followed Jesus. When Jesus died, he bravely asked Pilate for his body and laid him in his own new tomb in a garden, with Nicodemus. Lesson: be brave to show your love for Jesus, even when others are afraid!
2027-03-27.special: Great Saturday: blessing of new fire and water, renewal of baptismal promises (in many parishes); Resurrection service late tonight or before dawn.
term: Uyirppu

The Malayalam word for Resurrection; also the name of the Easter service in the Syro-Malabar Church, held at night or before dawn, when the Church proclaims that Christ is risen, the light and the bells return, and the Holy Qurbana of the Resurrection is celebrated.

family.explain: Today Jesus' body is resting in the tomb. The church is quiet, like a house waiting for someone to come home. When we were baptised, it was as if we went into the tomb with Jesus and came out with new life. Tonight we will sing: Jesus is risen!
family.intention: We pray for all who will be baptised this Easter, and we thank God for our own baptism.
family.ask: Ask: “Do you know the day you were baptised? Let us find out together.”

illus: An illustration

A mother in Thrissur told her children that Great Saturday is like the evening before a wedding. The house is quiet but full of preparation. Nobody is sad, but nobody is dancing yet either. The clothes are ironed, the food is ready, and everyone goes to bed early because tomorrow the bridegroom comes. Her six-year-old asked why they could not eat the Easter appam already, since it was ready. “Because,” she said, “we wait for him. When he comes, we eat together.” At three in the morning the child was the first one awake.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, resting in the tomb, we wait for you in faith with Mary your Mother. Amen.
share: God himself will provide the lamb (Genesis 22:8). Where do I need to trust God in the dark?
I called to the LORD out of my distress, and he answered me (Jonah 2:2). From what depth do I need to cry out?
We have been buried with him by baptism into death (Romans 6:4). What old habit must I leave in the tomb?
He is not here; for he has been raised (Matthew 28:6). Do I look for the living among the dead?
pm.resp: Lord, raise us with you to newness of life.
interc: For all who will be baptised this Easter, and for their godparents.
For the dead, especially those of our families, that they may rise with Christ.
For those who are waiting in darkness: in hospitals, in prisons, in grief.
For our parish, that the Uyirppu tonight may fill us with joy and courage.
For those who have stopped coming to church, that they may come home this Easter.
pm.close: Father, your Son rested in the tomb and went down among the dead to set them free. Keep us faithful in the waiting and raise us with him to new life. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: “Arise, shine; for your light has come”: Christ is the light risen over a dark world.
Hannah's song: God raises the poor from the dust, and raises his Son from the dead.
The empty tomb and the Lord who calls Mary by name: he is not here; he has been raised.
2027-03-28.action: Greet everyone today with the words: Christ is risen!
2027-03-28.question: Have I heard the Risen Lord call me by name, and to whom will I go and say: I have seen the Lord?
kidsaint: St Mary Magdalene

She loved Jesus very much and stayed near his cross. On Easter morning she went to his tomb crying, and Jesus called her by her name: “Mary!” She was the first to tell the apostles, “I have seen the Lord!” Lesson: Jesus knows your name too, and wants you to tell others about him!
2027-03-28.special: Easter Sunday: the Resurrection of our Lord. The Season of the Resurrection begins. The Great Fast ends.
term: Qyamta

The Syriac word for Resurrection, which gives its name to the Season of the Resurrection in the Syro-Malabar calendar: the seven weeks from Easter to Pentecost, a time of joy in the new life given by the Risen Christ.

family.explain: On Easter morning Mary Magdalene was crying at Jesus' tomb, because his body was gone. Then someone said her name: “Mary!” It was Jesus! He was alive! He had really died, and now he is risen and will never die again. Mary ran to tell the disciples: “I have seen the Lord!” Today we are happy because Jesus is alive and with us always.
family.intention: We thank Jesus for rising from the dead, and we pray for everyone who is sad today, that they may know he is alive.
family.ask: Ask: “Whom can we tell today that Jesus is alive, and how?”

illus: An illustration

A Syro-Malabar family in Mississauga had lost their father in the winter. On Easter night the mother almost stayed home: she could not bear the crowds and the singing. Her teenage daughter said, “Amma, Appa would want us there.” They sat in the back row in the dark. When the priest proclaimed the Resurrection and the lights came on, the little boy beside them, a stranger, turned and handed the mother his own candle, already lit. She said afterwards that it was the first moment since the funeral when she believed, not just knew, that her husband's story did not end in the cemetery. The flame passed from a child she did not know was the Easter Gospel for her.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, risen and living, we gather in your joy. Call each of us by name. Amen. Alleluia!
share: Arise, shine; for your light has come (Isaiah 60:1). What darkness in my life is the Risen Lord shining into?
He raises up the poor from the dust (1 Samuel 2:8). Where has God lifted me up?
Consider yourselves dead to sin and alive to God (Romans 6:11). What will I leave behind in the tomb?
Jesus said to her, “Mary!” (John 20:16). Have I heard him call my name?
pm.resp: Christ is risen! He is truly risen!
interc: For the Church throughout the world, that she may proclaim the Resurrection with joy and courage.
For the newly baptised, that they may live as children of the light.
For those who mourn this Easter, that the Risen Lord may call them by name.
For Christians who suffer persecution, that the hope of the Resurrection may strengthen them.
For our families, that our homes may be full of the peace and joy of the Risen Lord.
pm.close: Father, you raised your Son from the dead and opened for us the gate of eternal life. Make us witnesses of his Resurrection in word and deed, until we see him face to face. Through Christ our Lord. Amen. Alleluia!

quick: Abram went as the Lord told him, and built an altar wherever he camped.
Achan confessed; Hosea promises that the valley of trouble will become a door of hope.
Jesus asks a man ill for thirty-eight years: do you want to be made well?
2027-03-01.action: Name one long-standing sin or habit and take it to confession before Palm Sunday.
2027-03-01.question: Do I really want to be made well, or have I grown used to lying by the pool?

family.explain: There was a pool in Jerusalem where sick people waited for the water to move. One man had been ill for thirty-eight years, longer than most of our parents have been alive! Jesus asked him: do you want to be well? Then Jesus said: stand up, pick up your mat and walk. And he did! Jesus can heal what has been sick in us for a long time.
family.intention: We pray for those who have been ill for many years, and for those who look after them.
family.ask: Ask: “Is there something in our family that has needed healing for a long time? Let us ask Jesus about it tonight.”

illus: An illustration

An old man in Thamarassery, who came to the Malabar hills as a boy in 1952, used to tell his grandchildren about the first year. The family had no house, only a shelter of bamboo and palm leaf. But his father and the neighbours spent their first Sundays building a small chapel of mud and thatch, and a priest walked up from the valley once a month to offer the Holy Qurbana there. “We had nothing,” the old man said, “but we had an altar. That is why we stayed, and that is why we are still Christians.”

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you ask us whether we want to be made well. Here we are; heal us. Amen.
share: Go from your country (Genesis 12:1). Where is God asking me to go, or to let go?
Make confession to him; do not hide it (Joshua 7:19). What have I hidden from God for too long?
Do you want to be made well? (John 5:6). What excuses do I give instead of saying yes?
pm.resp: Lord, stand us up and make us walk.
interc: For the Church, a pilgrim people that carries the altar wherever she goes.
For migrants and settlers, that they may keep their faith in new lands.
For the Jewish people, first to hear the word of God, that they may grow in faithfulness to his covenant.
For those who have been ill for many years, and for their carers.
For our group, that we may not hide our sins but bring them to the light.
pm.close: Father, you called Abram and he went; you healed the man by the pool with a word. Call us, heal us, and make us walk in your ways. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Abram, afraid in Egypt, lied about Sarai; God protected her and kept his promise.
After confession, God sent Israel back to Ai: “Do not fear or be dismayed.”
Everything depends on God who shows mercy; the Son does what he sees the Father doing.
2027-03-02.action: Correct one half-truth you have told.
2027-03-02.question: When I am afraid, whom do I put at risk to protect myself?

family.explain: Abram was a great friend of God, but once he was very afraid. He asked his wife Sarai to tell a lie so that he would be safe. God protected Sarai anyway. Even good people make mistakes when they are afraid. God wants us to tell the truth and trust him.
family.intention: We pray for husbands and wives, that they may always protect each other.
family.ask: Ask: “When are we tempted to tell a small lie because we are afraid? What could we do instead?”

illus: An illustration

A young clerk in a bank in Thodupuzha made a small error in an account and covered it with a false entry. The false entry needed another, and soon he could not sleep. During the Lenten retreat he went to confession, and the priest told him gently that the confession was not finished until he told his manager. He went the next morning expecting to lose his job. The manager listened, corrected the entries with him, and said only: “Now I know I can trust you.”

pm.open: Lord, you show mercy to whom you will. We come with our fears and our failures; have mercy on us. Amen.
share: Say you are my sister (Genesis 12:13). Where has fear made me deceive or use someone?
Do not fear or be dismayed; go up now to Ai (Joshua 8:1). What place of defeat is God asking me to face again?
It depends on God who shows mercy (Romans 9:16). Do I treat my fast as a payment or as an opening to mercy?
pm.resp: Lord, have mercy on us.
interc: For the Church, that she may proclaim the mercy of God to all.
For husbands and wives, that fear may never make them betray one another.
For those who have fallen, that they may rise and try again.
For those who do not yet honour the Son, that they may come to know him.
For our group, that we may speak the truth in love.
pm.close: Father, everything depends on your mercy. Free us from fear, make us truthful, and teach us to do what we see your Son doing. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Mid-Lent: the fast reaches its midpoint; look back and begin again.
Abram let Lot choose first, and God gave Abram all the land he could see.
Many left when Jesus spoke of his flesh as true food; Peter said: to whom can we go?
2027-03-03.action: Take one step toward peace in a family quarrel, and renew one dropped Lenten resolution.
2027-03-03.question: Halfway through the fast, am I still walking with Jesus, or have I quietly turned back?

family.explain: Jesus told the people that he would give them his own body and blood as food. Many found this too hard and went away. Jesus asked his twelve apostles: do you want to go away too? Peter said: Lord, where would we go? Only you have the words that give eternal life. Jesus gives us this food at every Holy Qurbana.
family.intention: We pray for all who have given up their Lenten promises, that they may begin again.
family.ask: Ask: “Which of our Lenten promises have we forgotten? Let us start again today.”

illus: An illustration

Two brothers near Pala had not spoken for twelve years because of a boundary between their rubber plots, a strip of land only four metres wide. On Mid-Lent Wednesday the elder brother heard the reading about Abram and Lot. That evening he walked to his brother's house with the property papers and said: “Take the strip. We are brothers.” His brother cried. The next Sunday the two families sat together at the Holy Qurbana for the first time in twelve years.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, at the middle of the fast we come to you. To whom else can we go? Amen.
share: Let there be no strife between you and me; for we are kindred (Genesis 13:8). With whom am I not at peace?
Stretch out the sword that is in your hand (Joshua 8:18). Do I fight my battles alone, or under the Cross?
Do you also wish to go away? (John 6:67). Where am I tempted to turn back?
pm.resp: Lord, you have the words of eternal life.
interc: For the Church, that she may hold up the Cross before the world.
For families divided by quarrels over property, that they may be reconciled.
For those who have given up the fast, that they may begin again.
For those who find the teaching of the Holy Qurbana hard, that they may come to believe.
For our group, that we may stay with Jesus to the end.
pm.close: Father, at the middle of this fast we thank you for the days that are past and entrust to you the days that remain. Keep us with your Son, who has the words of eternal life. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Abram went after Lot, who had chosen Sodom, and brought him home.
Joshua built an altar and read the whole law to all the people, including women, children and strangers.
God has not rejected his people; Jesus waits for the Father's hour and goes up in secret.
2027-03-04.action: Contact one relative or friend who has drifted away, simply to show you care.
2027-03-04.question: Do I go after those who have strayed, or do I say: they chose it?

family.explain: Abram's nephew Lot had gone to live in a bad city. One day enemies captured him and took him away. Abram did not say: it is his own fault. He gathered his men, chased the enemies all through the night, and brought Lot home safely. God wants us to help people even when they have made wrong choices.
family.intention: We pray for members of our family who have drifted away from God.
family.ask: Ask: “Is there someone we know who needs us to go after them with kindness this week?”

illus: An illustration

A mother in Kanjirappally had a son who left home angry at twenty and stopped coming to church. Every Thursday for nine years she went to the parish adoration chapel and prayed for him, and every month she sent him a short message, never a sermon, only news of home and “we love you.” He told his own children later that the messages were the thread that held him. When he finally walked into the church on a Good Friday, she was in her usual place, and she simply moved over to make room.

pm.open: Lord, you go after the lost and gather your people around your word and your altar. Gather us now. Amen.
share: When Abram heard that his nephew had been taken captive, he went in pursuit (Genesis 14:14). Whom is God asking me to go after?
Joshua read every word before all the assembly, women and children and strangers (Joshua 8:35). Do I make room for others at the word and the altar?
There is a remnant, chosen by grace (Romans 11:5). Do I think I am the only faithful one left?
pm.resp: Lord, gather us into your people.
interc: For the Church, that she may go after every lost sheep.
For families with members who have drifted from the faith.
For the Jewish people, beloved of God for the sake of their fathers.
For children, that they may come to love the word of God and the Holy Qurbana.
For our group, that we may do our good works in secret, for the Father alone.
pm.close: Father, you never reject your people and you send your Son after those who stray. Make us faithful to your word and your altar, and bring back all who have wandered. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Abram believed when nothing had changed, and God passed alone between the pieces to seal his covenant.
Israel trusted mouldy bread and did not ask the Lord before signing.
God's call is irrevocable; Jesus, sent by the Father, waited for the hour that came on Friday.
2027-03-05.action: Keep the First Friday: confession, Holy Qurbana, and the consecration of your family to the Sacred Heart.
2027-03-05.question: What decision am I making with my own eyes alone, without asking the Lord?

family.explain: Abram was sad because he had no children. God took him outside at night and said: look up and count the stars! Your family will be as many as the stars. Abram believed God, even though he could not see it yet. Today is First Friday, when we remember that Jesus' Heart was opened for us on the Cross. His love is bigger than all the stars.
family.intention: We pray before the picture of the Sacred Heart for every member of our family.
family.ask: Ask: “What do we want to tell the Heart of Jesus tonight?”

illus: An illustration

A family in Ernakulam was close to selling their ancestral land to a smooth-talking buyer who offered more than anyone else and wanted the papers signed by Friday. It was the First Friday, and the grandmother insisted that they first pray before the Sacred Heart picture and ask the parish priest. They postponed the signing by one week. In that week a neighbour discovered that the same buyer had cheated three other families with forged documents. “The mouldy bread looked fresh,” the grandmother said, “but the Heart of Jesus saw through it.”

pm.open: Sacred Heart of Jesus, pierced for us, we come to you on this First Friday. Receive us and teach us. Amen.
share: Look toward heaven and count the stars (Genesis 15:5). Where do I need to believe when nothing has changed yet?
They did not ask direction from the LORD (Joshua 9:14). What decision have I made without praying?
O the depth of the riches and wisdom and knowledge of God! (Romans 11:33). When did I last simply praise God?
One of the soldiers pierced his side (John 19:34). What does the pierced Heart say to me today?
pm.resp: Sacred Heart of Jesus, we trust in you.
interc: For the Church, born from the pierced side of Christ.
For families consecrated to the Sacred Heart, that they may live that consecration.
For those making important decisions, that they may ask the Lord first.
For the Jewish people, whose call is irrevocable.
For our group, that we may believe in God's promises even in the dark.
pm.close: Father, you sent your Son, and on the Cross his Heart was opened for us. Seal us in your covenant, guide our decisions, and let us praise for ever the depth of your riches. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Paul: authority comes from God and is meant to serve the good; pay taxes, give respect, obey with conscience.
The limit: we must obey God rather than any human authority.
The police said: never has anyone spoken like this; Nicodemus asked that Jesus be given a hearing.
2027-03-06.action: When someone is criticised in their absence, ask that they first be heard.
2027-03-06.question: Do I condemn people without giving them a hearing?

family.explain: The leaders sent guards to arrest Jesus, but the guards came back without him. They said: no one has ever spoken like this man! Then a leader named Nicodemus said: we should listen to someone before we judge him. That was brave, because the others laughed at him. Later Nicodemus became a friend of Jesus in front of everyone.
family.intention: We pray for our country and for all who govern, that they may be honest and just.
family.ask: Ask: “When did we hear someone being blamed without being heard? What could we say next time?”

illus: An illustration

In a staff room in a school near Changanassery, the teachers were agreeing that a new colleague had taken money from the class fund. One older teacher, who said very little at staff meetings, put down her tea and said: “Has anyone asked her?” There was an awkward silence. The next day it turned out that the money had been taken to pay a sick student's hospital bill, with the principal's permission. The new teacher never forgot the one colleague who had asked for a hearing.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, never has anyone spoken like you. Open our ears to your word. Amen.
share: Let every person be subject to the governing authorities (Romans 13:1). Am I honest in my duties as a citizen?
Never has anyone spoken like this! (John 7:46). When did the word of Jesus last stop me in my tracks?
Our law does not judge people without first giving them a hearing (John 7:51). Whom have I judged without hearing?
pm.resp: Lord, give us ears to hear you.
interc: For the Church, that she may always obey God first.
For all who govern, in our country and our state, that they may serve the common good.
For those condemned without a fair hearing.
For all who seek Jesus by night, like Nicodemus, that they may find the courage to follow him openly.
For our group, that we may be honest citizens and fair judges.
pm.close: Father, all authority comes from you. Make us faithful citizens, fair in judgement and honest in our duties, and above all faithful to your Son, whose word is like no other. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Paul: food rules and feast days are a shadow; the substance belongs to Christ.
The rich ruler kept every commandment but would not follow when Jesus called.
The one thing lacking is not another rule but a Person: come, follow me.
2027-03-08.action: Give to the poor today what your fasting has saved.
2027-03-08.question: What is the one thing still lacking in my following of Christ?

family.explain: A rich young man asked Jesus how to go to heaven. He had kept all of God's rules. Jesus loved him and said: give your things to the poor and come with me. But the man loved his things too much, and he went away sad. Jesus wants to be more important to us than anything we own.
family.intention: We pray for the sick in hospitals, and for all who care for them, through the prayers of St John of God.
family.ask: Ask: “Is there one thing we own that we could share with someone who needs it this week?”

illus: An illustration

A retired teacher in Pala kept the Great Fast strictly for fifty years: no meat, no fish, one meal a day. She also kept a careful eye on her daughters-in-law, and could tell you who in the parish had eaten fish on a Friday. One Lenten evening her small granddaughter, filling the family's Lenten box for the poor with coins, asked her: Ammachi, who are we fasting for? The old woman began to answer, stopped, and said nothing for a long time. That year, the family remembers, she stopped counting other people's plates and began cooking for a sick neighbour instead.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you are the substance of all we hope for. Come and hold us together as your body. Amen.
share: The substance belongs to Christ (Colossians 2:17). Where has my religious practice become a shadow without substance?
There is still one thing lacking (Luke 18:22). What is the one thing the Lord is asking me to let go?
He became sad; for he was very rich (Luke 18:23). What riches, of money, comfort or reputation, make me sad when Jesus calls?
pm.resp: Lord, make us rich in you.
interc: For the Church, that her fasting may always lead to Christ and to charity.
For the sick and for all who serve in hospitals, through the prayers of St John of God.
For the poor who will receive the alms of our Lenten boxes.
For those who are rich, that they may be generous and free.
For our group, that we may follow when Jesus calls.
pm.close: Father, you have given us your Son, the treasure hidden in the field. Free our hearts from every lesser treasure, so that we may sell, give, and follow him with joy. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Paul: God gives seed to the sower; generous giving produces thanksgiving and communion.
The Samaritan did not ask who his neighbour was; he came near and showed mercy.
Jesus: Go and do likewise.
2027-03-09.action: Come near this week to one person you have been passing by.
2027-03-09.question: Whom have I passed by on the other side?

family.explain: A man was hurt by robbers and left on the road. Two important people saw him and walked past. Then a man from Samaria, a stranger, stopped. He cleaned the man's wounds, put him on his donkey, and paid for him to be looked after. Jesus says: be like him. A neighbour is anyone who needs our help.
family.intention: We pray for those who are hurt, alone or forgotten, and for all who help them.
family.ask: Ask: “Who needs our help this week, and what can we do for them together?”

illus: An illustration

On the national highway near Angamaly a motorcyclist lay on the road after an accident one evening. Cars slowed down; several people took videos on their phones; no one stopped. A migrant worker from Odisha, going home from a construction site, put down his bag, turned the injured man on his side as he had seen done, stopped an autorickshaw and went with him to the hospital, paying the fare from his day's wages. When the young man's family came, they wanted to thank him, but he had already gone back to his room. The parish priest told the story at the Lenten retreat that week, and simply read the Gospel after it.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, Good Samaritan of our souls, come near to us as we pray, and teach us to come near to others. Amen.
share: He who supplies seed to the sower (2 Corinthians 9:10). Do I give as one who sows, trusting God for the harvest?
When he saw him, he was moved with pity (Luke 10:33). When did I last let someone's suffering move me to act?
Go and do likewise (Luke 10:37). Who is the person on my road this week?
pm.resp: Lord, make us merciful.
interc: For the Church, that she may be an inn where every wounded person is cared for.
For victims of accidents and violence, and for those who stop to help them.
For migrant workers in our land, that they may be treated as neighbours.
For families, through the prayers of St Frances of Rome, that their homes may be open to the poor.
For our group, that we may not pass by on the other side.
pm.close: Father of mercies, your Son came down our road and bound up our wounds. Fill us with his compassion, make us generous sowers of good, and let our lives become thanksgiving for your indescribable gift. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Jude: even Michael left judgment to God; a life without fruit is a waterless cloud.
Jesus: let anyone without sin throw the first stone.
Mercy does not excuse sin; it lifts the sinner up and sends her into a new life.
2027-03-10.action: Put down one stone today: pray by name for someone you have condemned.
2027-03-10.question: Am I quicker to condemn others than to confess my own sin?

family.explain: Some men brought a woman to Jesus who had done something very wrong. They wanted to throw stones at her. Jesus said: whoever has never done anything wrong can throw the first stone. One by one they all went away, because everyone has done wrong things. Jesus told the woman: I do not condemn you; go, and do not do wrong again. Jesus forgives us too, and helps us to start again.
family.intention: We pray for all who will go to confession this Lent, that they may feel Jesus' mercy.
family.ask: Ask: “Is there someone we have been angry with, whom we can forgive tonight?”

illus: An illustration

In a family WhatsApp group in Thrissur a message arrived about a cousin whose marriage had broken down: a photo, a rumour, and a dozen comments within an hour. An elderly uncle who seldom wrote anything sent a single line: Let the one who has never sinned send the next message. The group went silent. That evening, instead of writing, he went to the cousin's house with a packet of jilebi from the bakery and sat with her for an hour, saying little. Months later she told her parish priest that his visit was the first time she had felt that God might still want her.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you do not condemn us but call us to a new life. Take the stones from our hands as we pray. Amen.
share: Waterless clouds carried along by the winds (Jude 12). Where do people find only a passing shadow in me, and no rain?
Let anyone among you who is without sin be the first to throw a stone (John 8:7). What stone am I holding?
Go your way, and from now on do not sin again (John 8:11). What sin do I need to leave behind this Lent?
pm.resp: Lord, have mercy on us.
interc: For the Church, that she may always be a place of mercy that calls to conversion.
For priests who hear confessions in these weeks of the fast.
For those whose sins have been made public, and who are judged by many.
For families broken by betrayal, that they may find healing.
For our group, that we may put down our stones and pray for one another.
pm.close: Father of mercy, your Son stood between the sinner and the stones. Give us his heart, free us from condemning others, and bring us to a true conversion of life. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Paul: train yourself in godliness; it holds promise for this life and the next.
Jesus foretells his Passion and Resurrection for the third time.
The disciples understood nothing; let us ask for eyes to see the meaning of the Cross.
2027-03-11.action: Choose one daily spiritual exercise and keep it every day until Easter.
2027-03-11.question: What am I really training myself for?

family.explain: Jesus told his friends that in Jerusalem people would hurt him and kill him, but that on the third day he would rise again. His friends did not understand. Soon we will remember these days in Holy Week. Let us ask Jesus to help us understand how much he loves us.
family.intention: We pray that our family may keep Holy Week well, and understand Jesus' love.
family.ask: Ask: “What is one good habit we can practise every day together until Easter?”

illus: An illustration

A schoolboy in Kannur joined the kalari near his house during the summer holidays. On the first morning the gurukkal made him do nothing but stand in the basic stance until his legs shook. On the tenth morning, the same. He complained to his grandfather, who had trained there fifty years before. The old man said: the stance is not the lesson; the stance is what makes every later lesson possible. That Lent the boy noticed that his grandfather prayed the same short prayers every morning on the veranda, without fail, and understood that this too was a stance.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you went up to Jerusalem for us. Train our hearts and open our eyes as we pray. Amen.
share: Train yourself in godliness (1 Timothy 4:7). What daily practice is forming my soul, and what is deforming it?
We have our hope set on the living God (1 Timothy 4:10). Where is my hope really set?
They understood nothing about all these things (Luke 18:34). What part of the mystery of the Cross do I still not understand?
pm.resp: Lord, open our eyes.
interc: For the Church, that she may be a good school of prayer and holiness.
For catechists and teachers who train the young in faith.
For young people, that they may train their bodies and their souls.
For those who do not understand the meaning of suffering in their lives.
For our group, that we may keep Holy Week with open eyes and hearts.
pm.close: Father, your Son went up to Jerusalem to suffer and to rise. Train us in godliness, set our hope on you, and give us light to understand his Passion, so that we may share his glory. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Abraham runs to welcome three strangers and receives God's promise: nothing is too wonderful for the Lord.
Caleb at eighty-five still follows the Lord wholeheartedly; Paul calls us to love and to put on Christ.
Jesus: before Abraham was, I am.
2027-03-12.action: Invite someone lonely to your table this week, and pray the Way of the Cross today.
2027-03-12.question: Who do I say that Jesus is, and does my life show it?

family.explain: One very hot day Abraham saw three visitors near his tent. He ran to welcome them, washed their feet, and gave them a good meal. They were messengers from God, and they told him that he and Sarah would have a baby boy, even though they were very old! God loves it when we welcome people, and nothing is too hard for God.
family.intention: We pray for grandparents and elderly people, that they may stay strong in faith like Caleb.
family.ask: Ask: “Whom can our family invite to our home before Easter?”

illus: An illustration

In a parish in Kottayam an eighty-six-year-old man was asked by the vicar to step down from leading the Friday Way of the Cross, so that he could rest. The old man agreed, and the next Friday he was there anyway, kneeling at the first station. Afterwards he said to the young man who had taken his place: I gave you the book, not my knees. Every Friday of that Lent he walked all fourteen stations with a stick, slower than the rest, and the young leader learned to wait for him before beginning each one.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you were before Abraham and you are with us now. Do not pass by your servants as we pray. Amen.
share: Is anything too wonderful for the LORD? (Genesis 18:14). What do I secretly think is too hard for God?
I wholeheartedly followed the LORD my God (Joshua 14:8). Is there a part of my heart that does not follow him?
Put on the Lord Jesus Christ (Romans 13:14). What work of darkness must I lay aside this week?
Before Abraham was, I am (John 8:58). What does it mean for my life that Jesus is truly God?
pm.resp: Lord, we believe in you.
interc: For the Church, that she may proclaim to all that Jesus is Lord and God.
For grandparents and elderly people, that they may remain strong in faith and be honoured in their families.
For all who are far from God, that like Augustine they may hear the call to take up and read.
For the Jewish people, the first to hear the word of God, and for friendship between Christians and Jews.
For our group, that we may be hospitable to everyone the Lord sends us.
pm.close: Father, you visited Abraham by the oaks of Mamre and kept your promise to him. Clothe us with Christ, your Son, the I AM, who was before Abraham; make us hospitable, wholehearted and loving, and bring us to rejoice in his day. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Paul: without love every gift is nothing; love is patient, kind, and never ends.
Jesus: from the beginning God made them one flesh; what God has joined, let no one separate.
Faith, hope and love abide, and the greatest of these is love.
2027-03-13.action: Read 1 Corinthians 13:4–7 with your own name in place of love, and practise one line today.
2027-03-13.question: Is my love patient and kind at home, where it is hardest?

family.explain: Paul tells us what real love looks like. Love is patient: it waits. Love is kind: it helps. Love is not jealous, not proud, not rude. Love does not always want its own way. Love does not get angry quickly and does not keep count of wrongs. When Mummy and Pappa love each other like this, and when we love one another like this, our home becomes a little piece of heaven.
family.intention: We pray for all married couples, especially for those who are having difficulties.
family.ask: Ask: “Which line of this reading is hardest for our family? Let us practise it this week.”

illus: An illustration

On their fiftieth wedding anniversary in a parish near Irinjalakuda, an old couple was asked by their grandchildren for the secret of a long marriage. The husband joked that he had learned to say only two words: Yes, dear. His wife laughed, and then said more seriously: we had many bad days. On the worst of them we still knelt together for the family prayer, even when we were not speaking to each other. Sometimes the Our Father was the only sentence we said to each other all day. But we said it together, and in the morning we started again.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you are love itself. Fill our hearts and our homes with your patient and kind love as we pray. Amen.
share: If I do not have love, I am nothing (1 Corinthians 13:2). Where am I doing good things without love?
Love is patient; love is kind (1 Corinthians 13:4). Who at home most needs my patience and kindness?
What God has joined together, let no one separate (Mark 10:9). How can I support the marriages in my family and parish?
pm.resp: Lord, teach us to love.
interc: For the Church, the Bride of Christ, that she may be faithful in love.
For married couples, that they may grow in patient and kind love.
For couples whose marriages are wounded or broken, and for their children.
For young people preparing for marriage.
For our group, that our love may be shown in deeds.
pm.close: Father, you made man and woman in your image and joined them as one flesh. Pour your love into our hearts by the Holy Spirit, strengthen every marriage and family, and lead us to see you face to face. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Paul lives because his people stand firm in the Lord.
Jesus came as light into the world, to save and not to condemn.
The word we refuse becomes our judge on the last day.
2027-03-15.action: Pray by name today for a family member who lives far away.
2027-03-15.question: Where am I still choosing to remain in the darkness?

family.explain: Jesus said: I came into the world like a light, so that no one who believes in me has to stay in the dark. When we are afraid in the dark, we switch on a lamp. When we are sad, or have done something wrong, Jesus is the light we can run to.
family.intention: We pray for family members and friends who live far from home.
family.ask: Ask: “Who in our family lives far away? Let us pray for them by name tonight.”

illus: An illustration

A mother in Thrissur kept a small oil lamp burning at the family prayer corner every evening of the fast, though her son had not called home from Dubai for two years after a quarrel. Her younger daughter asked why she bothered. “So that if he comes back, he will see that the light was never put out,” she said. On the Saturday before Hosanna Sunday the phone rang. He had gone to confession at a parish in Dubai, and the priest had told him to call his mother first.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, light of the world, shine on us now as we gather in your name. Amen.
share: For we now live, if you continue to stand firm in the Lord (1 Thessalonians 3:8). Whose faith keeps me alive, and whom do I strengthen?
I have come as light into the world (John 12:46). What part of my life still stays in the dark?
I came not to judge the world, but to save the world (John 12:47). Do I see Jesus as a judge to fear or a Saviour to trust?
pm.resp: Lord, let us not remain in the darkness.
interc: For the Church, that she may shine with the light of Christ.
For pastors and catechists, that their people may stand firm in the faith.
For families separated by work and study.
For those who are afraid to come back to the light.
For our group, that we may abound in love for one another and for all.
pm.close: Father, you sent your Son as light into the world. Strengthen our hearts in holiness and make us abound in love, so that we may welcome him with joy when he comes. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: The Lord knows how to rescue the godly, as he rescued Noah and Lot.
Jesus will not flee Herod; his road leads to Jerusalem and the third day.
He longs to gather us like a hen gathering her brood.
2027-03-16.action: Spend ten quiet minutes before the Blessed Sacrament this week.
2027-03-16.question: Am I willing to be gathered, or do I keep running from his wings?

family.explain: Jesus said he was like a mother hen. When a hawk comes, the hen calls her chicks and spreads her wings over them, so that they are safe. Jesus wants to keep us close and safe like that. But the chicks have to come when she calls!
family.intention: We pray for children who are lost or alone, that someone may gather them in.
family.ask: Ask: “When Jesus calls us this week, how can we run to him?”

illus: An illustration

After a fire in a farmyard in Kuttanad, the owner walked through the ashes and found a hen lying dead, burnt black. When he nudged her with his stick, three chicks ran out from under her wings, alive. She had stayed over them while the fire passed. The old man who told this story in his parish every Lent always ended the same way: “That is what he meant. He stayed over us while the fire passed.”

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you long to gather us under your wings. Here we are; gather us now. Amen.
share: The Lord knows how to rescue the godly from trial (2 Peter 2:9). Where do I need to be rescued?
Go and tell that fox (Luke 13:32). What threatens to turn me from the road God has set for me?
How often have I desired to gather your children together (Luke 13:34). Where have I been unwilling?
pm.resp: Lord, gather us under your wings.
interc: For the Church, that she may gather all peoples with the love of Christ.
For Christians who live among pressures that dull the conscience.
For the Jewish people, the first to hear the word of God, that they may grow in faithfulness to his covenant.
For children who are lost, unprotected or alone.
For our group, that we may not resist the Lord's call.
pm.close: Father, your Son longed to gather your children as a hen gathers her brood. Make us willing to be gathered, and rescue us in every trial. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: The commandment of love is old as creation and new in Christ.
Whoever hates a brother or sister walks in darkness and is blind.
Go privately to the one who has wronged you; aim to win them back.
2027-03-17.action: Speak gently to one person you have been avoiding.
2027-03-17.question: Whom have I lost because I never went to speak to them alone?

family.explain: Jesus said: if someone hurts you, go and talk to them quietly, just the two of you, and try to make peace. He also said: when two or three people pray together in my name, I am right there with them. So when our family prays together, Jesus is with us!
family.intention: We pray for families and neighbours who are not speaking to each other.
family.ask: Ask: “Is there anyone we need to make peace with before Easter?”

illus: An illustration

Two brothers in a village near Pala had not spoken for eleven years after dividing their father's land. Their houses stood forty metres apart. During the Lenten retreat the preacher read Matthew 18 and asked everyone to look at the person they would least like to sit beside. The younger brother saw the older one three rows ahead. That night he walked the forty metres with a packet of sugar, the way their mother used to send things between the houses. The older brother opened the door, looked at the sugar, and said only, “Come in, the tea is ready.”

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you promised to be among those gathered in your name. We are gathered; be among us now. Amen.
share: Whoever loves a brother or sister lives in the light (1 John 2:10). Where does a hidden resentment keep me in the dark?
Go and point out the fault when the two of you are alone (Matthew 18:15). Do I speak to people, or about them?
Where two or three are gathered in my name, I am there among them (Matthew 18:20). How can our group be a place where Christ is found?
pm.resp: Lord, make us one in your name.
interc: For the Church, that she may be a house of reconciliation.
For families divided by property and old quarrels.
For priests who hear confessions in these last days of the fast.
For the people of Ireland, through the prayers of St Patrick.
For our group, that we may agree in prayer and live in the light.
pm.close: Father, your Son promised to be among those gathered in his name. Heal our divisions, open our mouths to speak peace, and keep us in the light of love. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: False teachers are waterless springs: they promise and do not give.
A Christian heritage is a gift, but it cannot replace the fruit of a changed life.
John's answer: share your coat and your food.
2027-03-18.action: Give away clothes you do not wear before Pesaha.
2027-03-18.question: What would a thirsty person find if they came to me today?

family.explain: People asked John the Baptist: what should we do to please God? He gave a very simple answer: if you have two shirts, give one to someone who has none. If you have food, share it. That is how we show that we really love God.
family.intention: We pray for families who do not have enough clothes or food.
family.ask: Ask: “What can our family give away this week to someone who needs it?”

illus: An illustration

A college student in Ernakulam counted her clothes during the Great Fast, half as a joke, after hearing Luke 3:11 at Qurbana. She found thirty-one tops. She kept ten. The rest went in two bags to a home for migrant workers' families near the railway station. A girl there, about her own age, picked out a blue kurta and asked shyly if she could really keep it. The student said later that she had fasted for many Lents, but that was the first time she felt she had given something away and not just gone without.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, fountain of living water, fill us now, so that we may give to others. Amen.
share: These are waterless springs (2 Peter 2:17). Where do I promise much and give little?
Do not begin to say to yourselves, ‘We have Abraham as our ancestor’ (Luke 3:8). Do I rely on my family's faith instead of living my own?
What then should we do? (Luke 3:10). What is the concrete fruit the Lord asks of me this week?
pm.resp: Lord, make us bear good fruit.
interc: For the Church, that she may be a spring of living water for the thirsty.
For catechumens and all preparing for the sacraments at Easter, through the prayers of St Cyril of Jerusalem.
For those who have no coat and no food tonight.
For young people tempted by greed and empty promises.
For our group, that our faith may bear fruit in generous deeds.
pm.close: Father, you call us to bear fruits worthy of repentance. Train our hearts in generosity, and make us springs of living water for all who thirst. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Forty days complete: God remembered Abraham, and no intercession is wasted.
Jesus calls Lazarus out of the tomb and tells others to unbind him.
St Joseph did as the angel commanded, without a word.
2027-03-19.action: Make the Way of the Cross today, offering the forty days of your fast.
2027-03-19.question: What stone needs to be rolled away in me, and what bands still hold me?
catechism: Jesus, the resurrection and the life.
Lazarus and the Resurrection of Christ.
The holy family of Joseph and Mary.
kidsaint: St Joseph

Joseph was a carpenter in Nazareth, the husband of Mary and the foster father of Jesus. He worked hard, protected his family, and took them all the way to Egypt to keep baby Jesus safe. He never says a single word in the Bible, but he always did what God asked. Lesson: you can show your love for God by doing what is right, even without many words!
2027-03-19.special: Fortieth Friday of the Great Fast; feast of St Joseph.
term: Nalpatham Velli

The Fortieth Friday: the Friday on which the forty days of the Great Fast are completed, before the road leads on to Hosanna Sunday and the Week of the Passion. It is kept with the Way of the Cross, fasting and pilgrimage.

family.explain: Jesus' friend Lazarus had died and was buried in a cave with a big stone in front. Jesus told the people to move the stone, then he called in a loud voice: “Lazarus, come out!” And Lazarus walked out, alive! Jesus told the others to take off the cloths that were wrapped around him. Jesus has power over death, and at Easter he himself will rise.
family.intention: We pray for fathers today, through St Joseph, and for those who have died.
family.ask: Ask: “Can we do something kind for Appachan today, like St Joseph who cared for his family?”

illus: An illustration

A carpenter in Kanjirappally kept a small picture of St Joseph above his workbench, with a single line written under it: “He did as the angel commanded.” When his son, newly ordained, asked him why that line and not a prayer, the old man said: “Because in fifty years of work I have found that most of my prayers are answered by the same thing: get up in the morning and do the next right thing God asks.” On his feast the family still feeds three poor neighbours at that bench, an old man, a woman and a child.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you call the dead to life. Call us out of every darkness, through the prayers of St Joseph. Amen.
share: God remembered Abraham, and sent Lot out of the midst of the overthrow (Genesis 19:29). For whom have I stopped praying?
Welcome one another, therefore, just as Christ has welcomed you (Romans 15:7). Whom do I need to welcome before Easter?
Lazarus, come out! … Unbind him, and let him go (John 11:43–44). What binds me still, and who could help unbind me?
When Joseph awoke from sleep, he did as the angel of the Lord commanded him (Matthew 1:24). What is God asking me to do, simply and without delay?
pm.resp: Lord, you are the resurrection and the life.
interc: For the Church, through the prayers of St Joseph her patron.
For fathers, workers and all who provide for families.
For those buried in sin and despair, that they may hear Christ's voice.
For priests who will hear confessions in these last days of the fast.
For our group, that the forty days may bear fruit at Easter.
pm.close: Father, you remembered Abraham and raised Lazarus through your Son. Give us faith to see your glory, and the obedience of St Joseph to do your will. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Paul goes to Jerusalem as a captive to the Spirit, counting his life of no value.
It is more blessed to give than to receive.
Mary pours out her perfume, and the whole house is filled with its fragrance.
2027-03-20.action: Give one gift this week that costs you something.
2027-03-20.question: What will I pour out at the feet of Jesus in the coming week?

family.explain: Jesus went to visit his friends Martha, Mary and Lazarus. During dinner Mary took a jar of very expensive perfume and poured it on Jesus' feet, and the whole house smelled beautiful. She loved Jesus so much that she gave him her very best.
family.intention: We pray for our family as we get ready for Hosanna Sunday and the Week of the Passion.
family.ask: Ask: “What is the best thing we can give to Jesus this week?”

illus: An illustration

In a parish in Changanassery, an elderly widow brought a small bottle of attar to the sacristy on the Saturday before Hosanna Sunday every year. Her husband had brought it back from the Gulf the year before he died, and she used a drop each year on the linen for the altar of repose on Pesaha. The sacristan once asked why she did not keep it for herself. “It was the most precious thing he gave me,” she said. “Where else should it go?” For a whole evening every Pesaha, the side chapel smelled of that bottle.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, we sit with you at table, as Mary, Martha and Lazarus did. Receive what we bring. Amen.
share: I do not count my life of any value to myself, if only I may finish my course (Acts 20:24). What course has God given me to finish?
It is more blessed to give than to receive (Acts 20:35). When did I last give without counting the cost?
The house was filled with the fragrance of the perfume (John 12:3). What would fill my home with the fragrance of Christ this week?
pm.resp: Lord, receive our love.
interc: For the Church as she enters the Week of the Passion.
For pastors, that they may shepherd the flock obtained by Christ's blood.
For missionaries and all who have left home for the Gospel.
For the poor, who are always with us.
For our group, that our love for Christ may be generous.
pm.close: Father, as your Son came to Bethany six days before the Passover, he comes to our homes. Fill them with the fragrance of love, and make us generous at his feet. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Joseph, the beloved son, is sent by his father to his brothers, and they plot against him.
The tribes avoid a war by listening: one altar, one Lord, one people.
Caiaphas speaks better than he knows: Jesus will die to gather the scattered children of God.
2027-03-22.action: Before Pesaha, take the first step to heal one quarrel.
2027-03-22.question: Am I among those who plot, those who stand far off, or those the Son has gathered?
term: Hasha
The Syriac word for suffering. The Syro-Malabar Church calls Holy Week the Hasha week, from Hosanna Sunday to Easter.

family.explain: Jacob loved his son Joseph very much. One day he sent Joseph to find his brothers, who were looking after the sheep far away. Joseph said: Here I am. But his brothers were jealous, and when they saw him coming they planned to hurt him. Jesus is like Joseph: God the Father sent him to us, his brothers and sisters, even though he knew some would not welcome him.
family.intention: We pray for families who are divided by quarrels, that they may be reconciled before Easter.
family.ask: Ask: “Is there anyone in our family or among our neighbours we need to make peace with this week?”

illus: An illustration

Two brothers near Thodupuzha had not spoken for eleven years, all because of a boundary wall between their houses. Each blamed the other, and their children grew up as strangers. In Holy Week the parish kept the forty hours' adoration, and the younger brother signed up for the hour after midnight because he could not sleep. When he came in, he found his elder brother already kneeling in the front row. They prayed the hour side by side without a word. Outside, under the street light, the elder one said only: Come home on Thursday. On Pesaha evening the two families broke the appam at one table.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you came looking for your brothers and sisters. Find us now, and gather us into one. Amen.
share: Come, I will send you to them (Genesis 37:13). Where is God sending me this week, and do I answer, Here I am?
Far be it from us that we should rebel against the LORD (Joshua 22:29). Is there a misunderstanding I need to listen to before I judge?
to gather into one the dispersed children of God (John 11:52). Who is scattered from our family, parish or group, and how can I help bring them home?
pm.resp: Lord, gather us into one.
interc: For the Church in Hasha week, that she may walk with Christ to the Cross.
For families and parishes divided by quarrels, that they may be reconciled before Pesaha.
For the Jewish people, the first to hear the word of God, and for friendship between Christians and Jews.
For pilgrims at Malayattoor and all who keep the forty hours' adoration.
For our group, that we may answer the Father as Joseph did: Here I am.
pm.close: Father, you sent your beloved Son to look for his brothers and sisters, and he gave his life to gather your scattered children. Heal our divisions and keep us faithful this holy week. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Joseph is stripped, thrown into a dry pit and sold for twenty pieces of silver: jealousy grows into betrayal.
Christ, our high priest, prayed with loud cries and tears and learned obedience through suffering.
Unless a grain of wheat falls into the earth and dies, it remains alone; if it dies, it bears much fruit.
2027-03-23.action: Give up one comfort today for someone else's good, quietly and gladly.
2027-03-23.question: What am I keeping safe for myself that God is asking me to sow?

family.explain: Jesus held up a tiny grain of wheat and said: if you keep it in a box, it stays one little grain. But if you put it in the ground, it seems to die, and then it grows into a plant with many, many grains. Jesus was talking about himself: he would die on the Cross and rise again, and bring life to the whole world.
family.intention: We pray for our priests, and for anyone in our family who is jealous or hurt.
family.ask: Ask: “What is one thing each of us can give up this week so that someone else may be happy?”

illus: An illustration

An old farmer in Kuttanad used to keep the best paddy from each harvest in a separate bin for seed. One year, after a bad flood, the family had little to eat, and his grandson asked why they could not cook the seed paddy too. The old man said: if we eat it, we eat for one week; if we sow it, we eat for one year. That June he sowed every grain. On Pesaha night he told the story again at the family table, broke the appam, and added: Jesus did not keep himself for himself either.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, grain of wheat fallen into the earth, teach us to give our lives as you gave yours. Amen.
share: They sat down to eat (Genesis 37:25). Where have I been comfortable while someone near me suffered?
Today we know that the LORD is among us (Joshua 22:31). How can our trust in one another show that the Lord is among us?
Jesus offered up prayers and supplications, with loud cries and tears (Hebrews 5:7). Have I brought my tears to God in prayer?
Sir, we wish to see Jesus (John 12:21). Who around me wants to see Jesus, and how can I help?
pm.resp: Lord, let us bear much fruit.
interc: For the Church, that she may follow Christ on the way of the grain of wheat.
For priests and bishops, that they may be gentle with the ignorant and wayward.
For families divided by jealousy, property disputes or betrayal.
For those who seek Jesus without yet knowing him.
For our group, that we may not keep our lives for ourselves.
pm.close: Father, your Son was sold, stripped and buried like a grain in the earth, and you raised him to bear fruit for all nations. Make us generous with our lives, faithful to one another, and ready to follow him wherever he goes. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: In prison Joseph interprets the dreams of the cupbearer and the baker, and begs to be remembered; he is forgotten.
Christ, mediator of the new covenant, offered himself once for all; the Qurbana makes that one sacrifice present.
Troubled in soul, Jesus says: when I am lifted up from the earth, I will draw all people to myself.
2027-03-24.action: Prepare the Pesaha appam and paal together, and thank one person you have forgotten.
2027-03-24.question: Whom have I forgotten, and have I forgotten that the Lord remembers me?
term: Mar Thoma Sliva
The St Thomas Cross: the ancient cross of the St Thomas Christians, without a corpus, with blossoming arms and a dove above it, proclaiming the victory of the Cross and the gift of the Spirit.

family.explain: Joseph was in prison, though he had done nothing wrong. The king's cupbearer had a dream, and Joseph explained it: in three days you will be free. Joseph asked him: please remember me! But the cupbearer forgot. Jesus never forgets anyone. On the Cross a man asked him, Jesus, remember me, and Jesus promised him heaven that same day.
family.intention: We pray for prisoners, especially those who are innocent, and for everyone who feels forgotten.
family.ask: Ask: “Who has been kind to us whom we have forgotten to thank?”

illus: An illustration

A young engineer from Changanassery had studied with the help of a scholarship arranged by an old schoolteacher in his parish. He promised to visit her when he got his first job, and then, busy and far away, he forgot. On the Wednesday of Holy Week, home for Pesaha, he heard the reading at Qurbana: the chief cupbearer did not remember Joseph, but forgot him. That evening he went to her house with a packet of sweets. She was bedridden now, and she said she had prayed for him every night. On Pesaha night she ate the first piece of appam from his hand.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you remember us even when we forget you. Draw us to yourself now as we pray. Amen.
share: But remember me when it is well with you (Genesis 40:14). Whom have I forgotten now that things are well with me?
Be very careful, therefore, to love the LORD your God (Joshua 23:11). Where has my love for God grown careless?
he has appeared once for all to remove sin by the sacrifice of himself (Hebrews 9:26). How do I prepare to take part in that one sacrifice at the Qurbana?
when I am lifted up from the earth, will draw all people to myself (John 12:32). What draws me to the Cross, and what holds me back?
pm.resp: Lord, remember us in your kingdom.
interc: For the Church, that she may faithfully celebrate the memorial of the Lord's Passion.
For prisoners, especially the innocent and the forgotten.
For all who are preparing the Pesaha in their homes and parishes.
For those tempted, like Judas, to sell their faith for small gain.
For our group, that we may never forget the Lord who remembers us.
pm.close: Father, your Son was lifted up on the Cross to draw all people to himself, and he never forgets those who call on him. Keep us faithful in love, prepare our hearts for his Supper, and remember us in your kingdom. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Isaiah: the LORD will be your everlasting light; your days of mourning are ended.
Peter: David's tomb is with us; this Jesus God raised up, and we are witnesses.
Jesus: I will not leave you orphaned; because I live, you also will live.
2027-03-29.action: This evening, say to each one at home: The peace of the Lord be with you.
2027-03-29.question: Do I live as one who has been forgiven and made a dwelling of God?
kidsaint: St Peter the Apostle

Peter once denied Jesus three times because he was afraid. But after Jesus rose, Peter stood up in Jerusalem and told thousands of people: “This Jesus God raised up, and of that all of us are witnesses.” Lesson: Jesus can turn a frightened heart into a brave one!
2027-03-29.special: First Monday of Resurrection. Easter week, the week of the newly baptised.
term: Neophyte

From the Greek for ‘newly planted’: a person newly baptised. In the early Church the neophytes wore white garments all through Easter week and came daily to church to learn the meaning of the sacraments they had received.

family.explain: Before Jesus died, he told his friends: “I will not leave you alone. I am coming back to you.” And he did! He rose from the dead. He also said: “Because I live, you will live too.” And he gave them a special gift: his peace. That means a quiet, safe feeling in our hearts because Jesus is with us.
family.intention: We pray for children who feel alone or afraid, that they may know Jesus is with them.
family.ask: Ask: “When do you feel worried? Let us give that worry to Jesus and ask for his peace.”

illus: An illustration

A retired schoolteacher in Kottayam, a widow for ten years, used to say that she was never really alone in her house. Her neighbours thought it was the talk of an old woman. One day a young mother asked her how she could live so peacefully by herself. She pointed to the small crucifix and the Bible on her table. “When my husband died,” she said, “I read the words, ‘I will not leave you orphaned; I am coming to you.’ I decided to believe them. He has kept his promise every day.” The young mother began to visit her every Monday. She said later that she came to comfort the old teacher, and always went home comforted herself.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you promised not to leave us orphans. Come among us now and give us your peace. Amen. Alleluia!
share: The LORD will be your everlasting light (Isaiah 60:19). What mourning in my life does Easter end?
This Jesus God raised up, and of that all of us are witnesses (Acts 2:32). How am I a witness to the Resurrection?
Blessed are those whose iniquities are forgiven (Romans 4:7). Do I live as one who has been forgiven?
Because I live, you also will live (John 14:19). Where do I need the life of the Risen One today?
pm.resp: Lord, give us your peace.
interc: For the newly baptised, that they may persevere in the grace of their Baptism.
For orphans and those who feel abandoned, that they may know the love of the Father.
For the Jewish people, that God may bless them in his faithfulness, and for friendship between Christians and Jews.
For all who are troubled and afraid, that the peace of Christ may fill their hearts.
For our families, that the Father and the Son may make their home with us.
pm.close: Father, you raised your Son from the dead and gave him the promise of the Holy Spirit. Pour out that Spirit on us, make your home in us, and keep us in the peace of Christ. Through Christ our Lord. Amen. Alleluia!

quick: Isaiah: a garland instead of ashes, the oil of gladness instead of mourning.
Acts: the first Church devoted to teaching, fellowship, the breaking of bread and prayer.
Emmaus: Jesus walks with sad disciples, opens the Scriptures and is known in the breaking of bread.
2027-03-30.action: Walk with someone who is sad today: visit, call, or listen.
2027-03-30.question: Do I let the Risen Lord open the Scriptures to me, and do I recognise him in the Qurbana?
catechism: Emmaus and the shape of the Qurbana.
The four pillars of the first community.
kidsaint: St Cleopas

He was one of the two disciples who walked to Emmaus, sad because Jesus had died. A stranger walked with them and explained the Bible. When the stranger broke the bread at supper, they saw it was Jesus! They ran all the way back to Jerusalem to tell the others. Lesson: Jesus walks with us even when we are sad!
2027-03-30.special: First Tuesday of Resurrection. Easter week, the week of the newly baptised.
term: The Breaking of Bread

One of the oldest names for the Eucharist (Acts 2:42; Luke 24:35). In the Syro-Malabar Qurbana the priest breaks the consecrated Bread (the fraction) before Communion, as Jesus broke it at the Last Supper and at Emmaus.

family.explain: On Easter evening two friends of Jesus were walking home, very sad. Jesus came and walked with them, but they did not know it was him. He explained the Bible to them, and their hearts felt warm. When they sat down to eat, Jesus broke the bread, and suddenly they knew him! Jesus is with us too, in the Bible and in Holy Qurbana.
family.intention: We pray for people who are sad and lonely, that they may feel Jesus walking with them.
family.ask: Ask: “When did you feel that Jesus was close to you?”

illus: An illustration

A young nurse from Changanacherry working night shifts in a hospital in Dubai had stopped going to Qurbana. She was tired, far from home, and quietly angry with God about a broken engagement. One evening a Filipino colleague asked her to come with her to the Malayalam Qurbana in the parish, just to keep her company. She stood at the back. The Gospel was the walk to Emmaus. When the priest said, ‘But we had hoped’, she found herself crying, because that was exactly her prayer. When the Bread was broken at the altar, she said later, she knew he had been walking beside her all those months, like a stranger on the road. She went back the next Sunday, and this time she brought her colleague.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, walk with us now as you walked to Emmaus. Open the Scriptures to us and set our hearts on fire. Amen. Alleluia!
share: To give them a garland instead of ashes (Isaiah 61:3). What ashes in my life is the Lord turning into a garland?
Brothers, what should we do? (Acts 2:37). What is the Risen Lord asking me to do this Easter?
If Christ has not been raised, your faith is futile (1 Corinthians 15:17). Do I believe in the bodily Resurrection with my whole heart?
But we had hoped (Luke 24:21). What disappointed hope do I need to bring to the stranger on the road?
pm.resp: Lord, stay with us.
interc: For the Church, that she may be faithful to the apostles' teaching, the fellowship, the breaking of bread and the prayers.
For the newly baptised, that they may grow in the priesthood they have received.
For all who are disappointed and have lost hope, that the Risen Lord may walk with them.
For migrants and workers far from home, that they may find a community of faith.
For our parish, that every Qurbana may be an Emmaus for us.
pm.close: Father, your Son walked with his disciples on the road and was known to them in the breaking of bread. Open our eyes to see him, our hearts to burn with his word, and our feet to run and tell his Resurrection. Through Christ our Lord. Amen. Alleluia!

quick: Isaiah: you shall no more be called Forsaken but My Delight; as a bridegroom rejoices, so God rejoices over you.
Acts: threatened, the Church prays for boldness, and the place is shaken.
Jesus: I am the vine, you are the branches; apart from me you can do nothing.
2027-03-31.action: Spend ten minutes today simply abiding with Christ, in church or with the Gospel.
2027-03-31.question: Am I connected to the vine, or am I trying to bear fruit by myself?
kidsaint: St Benjamin the Deacon

He was a deacon in Persia about 1,600 years ago. The king put him in prison for teaching about Jesus, and then let him out on condition that he stop. But Benjamin said he could not stop telling people about Jesus, and he died as a martyr. Lesson: like the apostles, ask Jesus for courage to speak about him!
2027-03-31.special: First Wednesday of Resurrection. Easter week, the week of the newly baptised.
term: Parrhesia (boldness)
A Greek word used in Acts for the courage and freedom with which the apostles spoke of Christ (Acts 4:29, 31). It is a gift of the Holy Spirit, given in answer to prayer.

family.explain: Jesus said: “I am the vine, you are the branches.” A vine is a plant like the grape plant. The branches get all their life from the plant. If a branch is cut off, it dries up.
