If it stays on the plant, it grows grapes! We stay close to Jesus by praying, going to Holy Qurbana, and loving others. Then we can do good things, like a branch full of fruit.
family.intention: We pray that our family may always stay close to Jesus, like branches on the vine.
family.ask: Ask: “What can we do this week to stay close to Jesus?”

illus: An illustration

An old man in Kuravilangad kept a pepper vine climbing up a jackfruit tree behind his house. Every year after the harvest he cut it back hard, and his grandson, visiting from Bengaluru, thought he was destroying it. ‘Wait and see,’ said the grandfather. By the next season the vine was thick with green spikes of pepper. One evening the grandfather showed the boy a single branch that had been broken off in a storm and lay on the ground. It was dry and black. ‘Same vine, same rain, same sun,’ he said. ‘Only one thing was different: it was no longer attached.’ The boy remembered that when, years later, he found himself far from home and far from the Church, and he went back.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, true vine, we are your branches. Let your life flow in us as we gather in your name. Amen. Alleluia!
share: He has clothed me with the garments of salvation (Isaiah 61:10). Do I live as one clothed with Christ?
Grant to your servants to speak your word with all boldness (Acts 4:29). Where do I need courage to witness?
Bearing with one another in love (Ephesians 4:2). Whom do I find hard to bear with?
Abide in me as I abide in you (John 15:4). What helps me to abide, and what cuts me off?
pm.resp: Lord, keep us in your love.
interc: For the unity of the Church, that all Christians may be one in Christ.
For Christians persecuted for their faith, that they may be filled with the Holy Spirit and speak with boldness.
For the newly baptised, that they may remain in Christ and bear much fruit.
For those who are being pruned by suffering, that they may trust the Father's care.
For our parish, that it may be one body, bearing with one another in love.
pm.close: Father, you are the vinegrower who prunes the branches so that they may bear more fruit. Keep us in your Son, the true vine, fill us with the Holy Spirit, and make us one. Through Christ our Lord. Amen. Alleluia!

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, Hagar was a servant, a foreigner and a pregnant woman, treated harshly and alone in the desert. But the angel of the Lord found her by a spring of water and asked: where have you come from and where are you going? (Genesis 16:8). That is the question of the Great Fast for each of us.

Hagar gave God a name: El-roi, the God who sees (Genesis 16:13). The first person in the Bible to name God was a runaway slave woman. God sees those whom no one sees. Let us ask him to give us his eyes for the servants, the migrants and the hidden sufferers around us.

Israel discovered that the Gibeonites had tricked them, yet the leaders said: we have sworn to them by the Lord, and we must not touch them (Joshua 9:19). They kept their word even when it cost. Our vows and promises must be kept the same way. And the outsiders ended up carrying wood and water for the altar of the Lord: God brings strangers near.

Paul says: present your bodies as a living sacrifice, holy and acceptable to God (Romans 12:1). That is why we fast. Our eyes, tongue, hands and time are placed on the altar with Christ, and we are transformed by the renewing of our minds.

At the feast of Booths, when water was poured at the altar and great lamps lit up the temple, Jesus cried out: let anyone who is thirsty come to me; and he said: I am the light of the world (John 7:37; 8:12). Water and light are the signs of our Baptism.

This week, let us see one person we have overlooked, keep one promise we have delayed, offer one discipline as a living sacrifice, and come thirsty to Jesus. At Easter he will give us the living water and the light. Amen.
kids: Children, Hagar was alone in the desert and thought nobody cared. But God found her and she called him: the God who sees me! God sees you too, when you are happy and when you are sad.
Jesus said: if you are thirsty, come to me. He is like a spring of fresh water and a bright light in the dark. When you see water or a candle this week, remember Jesus!

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, at dawn the angels urge Lot to leave Sodom. But he lingered (Genesis 19:16). How often we too linger, knowing what we must leave. And the angels take him by the hand, the LORD being merciful to him, and bring him out. God's mercy does not wait for us to be brave.

They tell him: do not look back. But Lot's wife looked back, and became a pillar of salt (Genesis 19:26). She was out of the city, but her heart was still in it. Jesus says: remember Lot's wife (Luke 17:32). One week before Hosanna, what am I still looking back at?

Joshua tells Israel: not one of all the good promises of the LORD had failed; all came to pass (Joshua 21:45). And he gives them a charge: love the LORD, hold fast to him, and serve him with all your heart. God keeps every promise; let us keep faith with him.

Paul tells the Romans: the kingdom of God is not food and drink but righteousness and peace and joy in the Holy Spirit (Romans 14:17). Let us not judge how others fast, and let us never be a stumbling block. If my drink or my habit makes my brother fall, love tells me to give it up.

Jesus says: I am the good shepherd; the good shepherd lays down his life for the sheep (John 10:11). No one takes his life from him; he lays it down of his own accord, and takes it up again. Next week we will see him do it.
Let us pray for our shepherds, our bishops and priests. Let us pray for the unity of all the sheep. And let us follow the voice of the Good Shepherd as he walks toward Jerusalem for us. Amen.
kids: Children, Lot was slow to leave a bad city, so the angels took him by the hand and led him out. God takes our hand too when we are slow to do good!
Jesus is our Good Shepherd. He knows each of us by name, and he loves us so much that he gave his life for us. Let us listen to his voice!

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, today we carried blessed palms and sang Hosanna, as the crowds did on the road into Jerusalem. The Great Fast now gives way to the Week of the Passion. The palms we take home will be folded into a cross for the Pesaha appam, and next year they will become the ashes of a new Great Fast.

Long ago Jacob blessed his son Judah: the scepter shall not depart from Judah (Genesis 49:10). And he spoke of a donkey's colt bound to the vine. Today the Son of David from the tribe of Judah comes riding on that colt.

Zechariah tells us what kind of King he is: lo, your king comes to you; triumphant and victorious is he, humble and riding on a donkey (Zechariah 9:9). He does not come on a war horse. He comes to command peace to the nations and to set free the prisoners of hope by the blood of the covenant.

Paul warns us Gentile Christians not to boast: it is not you that support the root, but the root that supports you (Romans 11:18). This week we will hear the Passion. Let us never blame the Jewish people for the death of Jesus. He died for the sins of all of us.

The crowds cried: Hosanna to the Son of David! Blessed is the one who comes in the name of the Lord! (Matthew 21:9). Hosanna means save us, we pray. Then Jesus cleansed the temple: my house shall be called a house of prayer (Matthew 21:13). He healed the blind and the lame, and the children went on singing.

The same crowd that sings Hosanna today will shout Crucify on Friday. Let our Hosanna last all week. Let our homes be houses of prayer, let us come to Pesaha, to Passion Friday and to the Easter Qurbana, and let us follow our humble King to the Cross and to the empty tomb. Amen.
kids: Children, today we waved palm leaves and sang Hosanna, just like the children in Jerusalem! Jesus loved hearing their praise.
Jesus came riding on a little donkey, not on a big war horse, because he is a gentle King of peace. Take your blessed palm home and keep it near the cross in your prayer corner.

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, tonight is Pesaha. In Egypt, on the night of the Passover, each family took a lamb without blemish, put its blood on the doorposts, and ate it with unleavened bread, ready for the journey. God said: when I see the blood, I will pass over you (Exodus 12:13). That night became a day of remembrance for ever.

Tonight the true Lamb sits at table with his friends. Our paschal lamb, Christ, has been sacrificed (1 Corinthians 5:7). His blood is not painted on our doors; he gives it to us to drink. And Malachi's promise is fulfilled: from the rising of the sun to its setting a pure offering is made to God's name, at every altar where the Qurbana is celebrated.

On the night he was betrayed, the Lord took bread, gave thanks, broke it and said: this is my body that is for you. Do this in remembrance of me. He took the cup and said: this is my blood of the covenant, poured out for many for the forgiveness of sins. He did not say this is a sign. He said this is my body. That is the faith of the Church: Christ is truly present, and his one sacrifice is made present on our altar.

Tonight we thank God for our priests. When the Lord said, Do this in remembrance of me, he made his apostles priests of the new covenant. Pray for the priest who will stand at our altar tonight, and for the priests who baptized you and absolved you.

Then the Lord did something no master ever did. He got up from the table, tied a towel around himself, and washed his disciples' feet, even the feet of Judas. Peter said: you will never wash my feet. Jesus said: unless I wash you, you have no share with me (John 13:8). We too must let him wash us, in confession and in his mercy.

And he said: if I, your Lord and Teacher, have washed your feet, you also ought to wash one another's feet (John 13:14). The altar and the basin belong together. Tonight, when the priest kneels before twelve of our people, remember who knelt first; and tomorrow, in your home and your work, kneel in the same way.

Tonight we will break the Pesaha appam in our homes, dip it in the paal and share it from the eldest to the youngest. It is not a second Qurbana, but it keeps our homes united around the Lord's Supper. Then let us not sleep too soon. The Lord asks: could you not stay awake with me one hour? Let us watch with him. Having loved his own, he loved them to the end. Amen.
kids: Children, at the Last Supper Jesus gave us himself in the Holy Qurbana. He said: this is my body. That is why we are so quiet and careful when we receive him!
Then Jesus washed his friends' feet, like a servant. Tonight, can you help at home without being asked, to show Jesus' love?

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, today there is no Qurbana. The altar is bare and the tabernacle is empty. The Church stands in silence at the foot of the Cross, where the one Sacrifice was offered once for all.

We began with Abraham and Isaac on the mountain. The boy asked, “Where is the lamb for a burnt offering?” and his father answered, “God himself will provide the lamb.” On Moriah the knife was stopped. On Calvary it was not. The Father gave his only Son, whom he loves, and the Son carried the wood of his own sacrifice.

Isaiah saw him centuries before: “He was wounded for our transgressions, crushed for our iniquities… and by his bruises we are healed.” He did not open his mouth. And Paul tells us why: “God proves his love for us in that while we still were sinners Christ died for us.” Not for the good, but for sinners. For you and for me.

Listen to his words from the Cross. “Father, forgive them.” He forgives those who are killing him. “Today you will be with me in Paradise.” He opens heaven to a thief. “Here is your mother.” He gives us Mary. “I am thirsty.” He thirsts for our love. “It is finished.” Not ‘I am finished’, but ‘the work is complete’.

Who killed him? The Church answers honestly: not a people, not a nation, but sin, our sin. That is why today we do not point at anyone. We beat our own breasts, and then we come to kiss the wounds that heal us.

When you take the bitter drink today, remember the thirst of the Lord. Do not run from the bitterness of your own cross. Stand with Mary, forgive someone by name, and keep this evening in silence. We adore you, O Christ, and we bless you, because by your holy Cross you have redeemed the world. Amen.
kids: Children, today Jesus died on the cross. He did it because he loves us so much and wanted to take away all our sins.
On the cross Jesus said sorry for the people who hurt him: ‘Father, forgive them.’ Can you forgive someone today?
When we kiss the cross today, let us say: ‘Thank you, Jesus, for loving me so much!’

homily: Dear friends, today is the day of the great silence. The Lord lies in the tomb. The disciples hide in fear. Only Mary waits in faith. And yet the Church says that today something tremendous is happening: Christ goes down among the dead to seek Adam and all his children.
We read again of Abraham and Isaac. Isaac came down the mountain alive, as if received back from the dead. Abraham believed that God could even raise the dead. Today we wait with that same faith.

Jonah prayed from the belly of the fish: “I called to the LORD out of my distress, and he answered me.” Jesus said: as Jonah was three days in the fish, so the Son of Man will be three days in the heart of the earth. Death has swallowed him, but it cannot keep him.

Paul tells us that we are part of this story. When we were baptised, we were buried with Christ, so that we might rise with him and walk in newness of life. Today we renew our baptismal promises. We say no again to Satan and his works, and yes to the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit.

And the Gospel already lets us hear the morning: the earth shakes, the stone is rolled away, and the angel says, “He is not here; for he has been raised, as he said.” The Risen Lord sends us to all nations, and promises: “I am with you always.”
So let us keep this day quietly, prepare our homes and our hearts, and come tonight to the Uyirppu, all of us, even the sleepy children. The bridegroom is coming. Amen.
kids: Children, today Jesus is resting in the tomb. The church is quiet, like a house waiting for someone special to come home.
When you were baptised, you got new life from Jesus. Ask your parents today: on what day was I baptised?
Tonight we will hear the best news ever: Jesus is risen! Get ready to sing Alleluia!

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, Christ is risen! He is truly risen! This night the darkness of the church was broken by light, and we heard Isaiah say: “Arise, shine; for your light has come, and the glory of the LORD has risen upon you.” The light that has come is not a sunrise. It is a Person. Jesus is alive.

We sang with Hannah: “The LORD kills and brings to life; he brings down to Sheol and raises up.” She sang it for a child born to a barren woman. We sing it for the Son raised from the tomb. God has done the greatest reversal of all: the condemned is vindicated, the crucified is Lord.

The women came to the tomb in the dark. The stone was rolled away, and the angel said: “He is not here; for he has been raised, as he said. Come, see the place where he lay.” The tomb is empty, not because someone took his body, but because he is risen in his body, the same body that bore the wounds.

And Mary Magdalene, weeping in the garden, thought he was the gardener. Then he said her name: “Mary!” And she knew him. That is Easter: not an idea, not a memory, but a living Lord who knows his own by name.

Paul tells us what this means: “consider yourselves dead to sin and alive to God in Christ Jesus.” Easter happened to Jesus, and through Baptism it has happened to us. Let us not go back to the tomb we have left. Let us walk in newness of life.

Today we break the fast. Let us do it with joy, and let no one be alone at Easter: share your table, visit the lonely, forgive the one who hurt you. And like Mary Magdalene, let us go and tell someone: I have seen the Lord. Christ is risen! Alleluia! Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus is alive! On Easter morning his tomb was empty, because God raised him from the dead.
Mary Magdalene was crying, and Jesus called her by her name: ‘Mary!’ Jesus knows your name too!
Today let's say to everyone we meet: ‘Jesus is risen! Alleluia!’

homily: Dear friends, God says to Abram: go from your country and your kindred and your father's house to the land that I will show you (Genesis 12:1). Abram is seventy-five, the map is blank, and yet he goes. At every place he pitches his tent, he builds an altar. A Christian life is a journey with an altar at every stop.

Achan had hidden stolen things in his tent. When the truth comes out, Joshua says: my son, give glory to the Lord and make confession; do not hide it from me (Joshua 7:19). The place of his punishment was called the Valley of Achor, the valley of trouble. But God promised through Hosea to make the Valley of Achor a door of hope (Hosea 2:15). Confession is that door.

Paul speaks of his people Israel with great sorrow and great love, for to them belong the covenants, the worship and the promises, and from them comes the Messiah (Romans 9:4–5). We learn from him to honour the people of the first covenant.

By the pool lies a man who has been ill for thirty-eight years. Jesus asks him: do you want to be made well? (John 5:6). He answers with an excuse. Jesus answers with a command: stand up, take your mat and walk. Halfway through this fast, Jesus asks us the same question. Let us not answer with excuses. Amen.
kids: Children, a man had been sick for thirty-eight years, and Jesus asked him: do you want to be well? Then Jesus said: stand up and walk, and he did! Is there something you would like Jesus to make well in you? Tell him tonight.

homily: Dear friends, Abram, who left everything in faith, becomes afraid in Egypt. He tells his wife: say you are my sister, so that my life may be spared (Genesis 12:13). The father of faith tells a half-lie, and Sarai pays the price. But God protects her and keeps his promise.

After Achan's confession, God says to Joshua: do not fear or be dismayed; go up now to Ai (Joshua 8:1). God sends him back to the very place of defeat. After a good confession, God often sends us back to the same weak place, but now he goes with us.
Paul says: it depends not on human will or exertion, but on God who shows mercy (Romans 9:16). Our fast does not buy God's mercy; it opens our hearts to receive it.

Jesus says: the Son does whatever he sees the Father doing, so that all may honour the Son just as they honour the Father (John 5:19, 23). Let us honour him today, at the altar and in our lives, and do what we see him doing. Amen.
kids: Children, Abram was afraid and told a lie, but God still took care of everyone. When you are afraid, do not tell a lie: tell Jesus you are afraid, and tell the truth. He will help you!

homily: Dear friends, today is Mid-Lent, the middle of the Great Fast. It is a good day to look back honestly and to begin again.

Abram and Lot quarrel over land. Abram, the elder, says: let there be no strife between you and me, for we are kindred (Genesis 13:8), and he lets Lot choose first. Then God gives Abram all the land he can see. Many families carry the wound of a quarrel over property. Today, let us take one step toward peace.

Joshua stretches out his hand toward Ai and does not lower it until the battle is won. The Fathers saw in this outstretched hand a picture of Christ's arms stretched out on the Cross. At the middle of the fast, the Church holds up the Cross: our battle has already been won by him.

When Jesus says his flesh is true food, many disciples leave him. He asks the Twelve: do you also wish to go away? Peter answers: Lord, to whom can we go? You have the words of eternal life (John 6:68). If we are tired today, let us make Peter's answer our own, and walk on to Easter. Amen.
kids: Children, when some people left Jesus, he asked his friends: will you leave me too? Peter said: Lord, where would we go? We want to stay with you! Let us tell Jesus today: I want to stay with you too.

homily: Dear friends, Lot chose to live near Sodom, and when enemies captured him, Abram did not say: it is his own fault. He took his men, went in pursuit as far as Dan, and brought Lot home (Genesis 14:14–16). Is there a Lot in our family? Let us go after him with prayer and with love.

After the battle, Joshua builds an altar and reads every word of the law before all the people, the women, the little ones and the strangers (Joshua 8:35). This is the shape of our Holy Qurbana: the word read to all, and the offering on the altar. Let us bring our children, and help them hear.
Paul says: God has not rejected his people whom he foreknew (Romans 11:2). God keeps a remnant chosen by grace. We honour the Jewish people, and we never think that we alone are faithful.

Jesus' relatives want him to go and make a name for himself. He says: my time has not yet come, and he goes up to the feast in secret (John 7:6, 10). In this fast, let us also do our good in secret, and trust the Father's time. Amen.
kids: Children, Abram's nephew got into big trouble because of his own choices, but Abram still went to rescue him! Can you be kind today to someone who has been naughty or unkind? That is what Jesus does for us.

homily: Dear friends, Abram is tired and childless. God takes him outside and says: look toward heaven and count the stars; so shall your descendants be. And he believed the Lord; and the Lord reckoned it to him as righteousness (Genesis 15:5–6). Faith believes before it sees.

Then God makes a covenant. A smoking fire pot and a flaming torch pass between the pieces of the animals. Only God passes; only God binds himself. On the Cross, God kept this covenant at the cost of his Son, and the soldier's spear opened the Heart from which blood and water flowed.
The Gibeonites deceive Israel with mouldy bread, and the leaders did not ask direction from the Lord (Joshua 9:14). Before we make our big decisions, let us bring them to the Heart of Jesus.

Paul says that the gifts and the calling of God are irrevocable, and he cries out: O the depth of the riches and wisdom and knowledge of God! (Romans 11:29, 33). On this First Friday, let us go to confession, receive the Lord, and renew our trust in his Sacred Heart. Amen.
kids: Children, God told Abram to count the stars, because his family would be just as big! Abram could not count them all, and God's love for you is even bigger. Tonight, look at the stars, or at the picture of the Sacred Heart, and say: Jesus, I trust in you.

homily: Dear friends, Paul writes: let every person be subject to the governing authorities; for there is no authority except from God (Romans 13:1). Authority is meant to be God's servant for our good. So a Christian pays tax honestly, refuses bribes, gives respect and prays for those who govern.

But there is a limit. When the authorities forbade the apostles to preach, Peter said: we must obey God rather than any human authority (Acts 5:29). We give to the emperor what is his, and to God what is God's.

The guards sent to arrest Jesus came back empty-handed and said: never has anyone spoken like this! (John 7:46). They had only listened. If we listen to Jesus with open hearts during this fast, his word will stop us too.

Nicodemus asked the council: does our law judge people without first giving them a hearing? (John 7:51). It was a small act of courage, and it grew until he came openly to bury the Lord. Let us also defend those who are judged without a hearing. Amen.
kids: Children, the guards went to catch Jesus, but when they heard him speak they came back and said: no one ever talked like this man! Let us listen to Jesus too. And when someone is being blamed, let us say: let's hear their side first!

homily: Dear friends, Paul warns the Colossians: do not let anyone condemn you in matters of food and drink or of festivals; these are only a shadow of what is to come, but the substance belongs to Christ (Colossians 2:16–17).

We fast seriously in this Great Fast, as our forefathers did. But the fast is a shadow cast by Christ. If it makes us proud, or makes us judge our neighbour's plate, we have kept the shadow and lost the substance. Let our fast bind us to Christ, our Head, and to one another.

A rich ruler had kept all the commandments since his youth. Jesus told him: there is still one thing lacking; sell all that you own, give to the poor, and come, follow me (Luke 18:22). The man went away sad, for he was very rich.

The one thing lacking is not another rule; it is Jesus himself. St John of God gave away his books and spent his life carrying the sick poor. What holds my heart? This week let us give what our fast has saved, and follow him more closely. Amen.
kids: Children, a rich man asked Jesus how to go to heaven. Jesus said: share what you have with the poor and come with me. But he loved his things too much and went away sad. Can you share one of your things with someone this week, and stay close to Jesus?

homily: Dear friends, Paul tells the Corinthians that God supplies seed to the sower and bread for food, and will multiply the harvest of our righteousness (2 Corinthians 9:10). When we give alms in this Great Fast, we are not paying God a tax. We are sowing in his field.

And the harvest is more than bread for the hungry: it is thanksgiving to God, and prayer and love between people who were strangers. That is why Paul ends with a cry of praise: thanks be to God for his indescribable gift! (2 Corinthians 9:15).

In the Gospel a priest and a Levite pass by a wounded man. But a Samaritan, a stranger, sees him and is moved with pity. He bandages his wounds, pours oil and wine, carries him to an inn and pays for his care (Luke 10:33–35).

Jesus says to us: go and do likewise (Luke 10:37). St Frances of Rome opened her house to the poor during famine and plague. This week, let us come near to one person we have been passing by. That is how the fast becomes mercy. Amen.
kids: Children, a man was hurt and lying on the road. Two people walked past, but a kind stranger stopped and helped him. Jesus says: be like that kind man. Who can you help this week, even in a small way?

homily: Dear friends, Jude reminds us that even the archangel Michael did not dare to condemn the devil, but said: the Lord rebuke you (Jude 9). Judgment belongs to God. And he warns us not to become waterless clouds and autumn trees without fruit (Jude 12): lives that promise and do not give.
In the temple some scribes and Pharisees bring Jesus a woman caught in adultery. They do not care for her; they want to trap him. Jesus bends down and writes on the ground.

Then he says: let anyone among you who is without sin be the first to throw a stone at her (John 8:7). One by one they go away, beginning with the elders. Only two are left, as St Augustine says: misery and mercy.

Jesus tells her: neither do I condemn you; go your way, and from now on do not sin again (John 8:11). This is what happens in confession. This week, let us put down our stones, go to confession, and begin again. Amen.
kids: Children, some people wanted to throw stones at a woman who had done wrong. Jesus said: only someone who has never done wrong may throw a stone. Everyone went away! Jesus forgave her and said: go, and do not do wrong again. Jesus forgives us too when we say sorry.

homily: Dear friends, Paul tells Timothy: train yourself in godliness; physical training is of some value, but godliness is valuable in every way, holding promise for both the present life and the life to come (1 Timothy 4:7–8).

The Great Fast is a season of training. The same prayers every day, the same small sacrifices at table, the same Way of the Cross each Friday: slowly they give the soul new habits. We train not to impress others, but because our hope is set on the living God.

In the Gospel Jesus tells the Twelve: we are going up to Jerusalem; the Son of Man will be mocked, insulted, spat upon, flogged and killed, and on the third day he will rise again (Luke 18:31–33). But they understood nothing (Luke 18:34).

We too can know the Passion story by heart and still not understand it. In ten days we enter the Great Week. Let us ask, like the blind man of Jericho, for eyes to see that the way of the Cross is the way to glory. Amen.
kids: Children, sportsmen practise every day to become strong. Jesus' friends also need to practise: praying every day and doing good things every day. What good thing will you practise every day until Easter?

homily: Dear friends, in the heat of the day Abraham sees three strangers and runs to welcome them: my lord, do not pass by your servant (Genesis 18:3). He serves them a feast, and receives God's promise of a son. When Sarah laughs, the Lord asks: is anything too wonderful for the LORD? (Genesis 18:14).

Caleb, at eighty-five, says: I am still as strong today as I was on the day that Moses sent me, and asks for the hardest hill country, because he has wholeheartedly followed the Lord (Joshua 14:8–12). Faith does not retire.

Paul tells us: owe no one anything, except to love one another; the night is far gone, the day is near; put on the Lord Jesus Christ (Romans 13:8, 12, 14). These were the words that converted St Augustine in a garden in Milan.

And Jesus says: very truly, I tell you, before Abraham was, I am (John 8:58). He is God, the same who spoke to Moses from the bush. On this Friday of the fast, as we walk the Way of the Cross, let us kneel before him and say: my Lord and my God. Amen.
kids: Children, Abraham ran to welcome three visitors and gave them food, and they were God's messengers! When we welcome people kindly, we welcome God. And Jesus tells us that he was alive even before Abraham, because he is God!

homily: Dear friends, Paul tells a divided parish in Corinth: if I speak in the tongues of mortals and of angels, but do not have love, I am a noisy gong or a clanging cymbal (1 Corinthians 13:1). Without love, every gift is nothing.

Love is patient; love is kind; it does not insist on its own way; it bears all things, believes all things, hopes all things, endures all things (1 Corinthians 13:4–7). Put your own name in place of love, and see where you must grow this Lent.

In the Gospel Jesus goes back to the beginning: God made them male and female, and the two become one flesh. Therefore what God has joined together, let no one separate (Mark 10:6–9). Christian marriage is a gift of grace, and Christ gives the strength to live it.

Let us pray today for all married couples, especially those who are struggling, and for those whose marriages are broken, who remain our brothers and sisters. Faith, hope and love abide, and the greatest of these is love (1 Corinthians 13:13). Amen.
kids: Children, Paul says that love is patient and kind, and does not always want its own way. Can you be patient and kind with your brothers, sisters and parents today, even when it is hard?

homily: Dear friends, Paul had left the young Church in Thessalonica too soon, and he was afraid for them. When Timothy returns with news of their faith and love, Paul says: for we now live, if you continue to stand firm in the Lord (1 Thessalonians 3:8).

That is the heart of every parent, teacher and priest. We live when those we love stand firm. Paul prays that the Lord will make them increase and abound in love, and strengthen their hearts in holiness (1 Thessalonians 3:12–13). Let us pray the same for our children and for family members far from home.
In the Gospel Jesus cries aloud: I have come as light into the world, so that everyone who believes in me should not remain in the darkness (John 12:46). He did not come to judge but to save.
Yet the word we refuse will one day be our judge. Hosanna Sunday is near. Let us not remain in the darkness: let us bring what is hidden to the light of confession this week. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus said: I came like a light into the world. When it is dark we need a lamp. Tonight, when you see a light at the prayer corner, remember that Jesus is the light for your heart.

homily: Dear friends, Peter reminds his readers that God saved Noah and rescued Lot, a righteous man tormented by the lawless deeds he saw and heard every day. Then the Lord knows how to rescue the godly from trial (2 Peter 2:9).
Lot was troubled by the evil around him; he had not grown used to it. Let us ask whether our conscience is still awake, or whether we have quietly made peace with what is wrong.

In the Gospel Jesus is warned that Herod wants to kill him. He will not run: he must go on to Jerusalem. And he weeps over the city: how often have I desired to gather your children together as a hen gathers her brood under her wings (Luke 13:34).
This is the grief of love, and it is spoken to every heart that refuses to be gathered, including ours. On the Cross he spread his arms like wings over us. This week, let us come under them. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus said he is like a mother hen who keeps her chicks safe under her wings. When you are afraid, run to Jesus in prayer, and he will hold you close.

homily: Dear friends, John says that the commandment of love is old, given from the beginning, and also new, because in Christ the darkness is passing away and the true light is already shining (1 John 2:8).

He is blunt: whoever says he is in the light while hating a brother or sister is still in the darkness (1 John 2:9). We can fast, pray and come to church every day, and still walk in darkness if we keep a quarrel alive.

Jesus shows the way: if someone sins against you, go and speak to them alone. If they listen, you have regained that one (Matthew 18:15). The aim is not to win an argument but to win back a brother or sister.
Then he promises: where two or three are gathered in my name, I am there among them (Matthew 18:20). Before Pesaha, let us take the first step toward someone we have been avoiding. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus said that when two or three people pray together in his name, he is right there with them. If you have quarrelled with a brother, sister or friend, make peace today, and then pray together. Jesus will be with you!

homily: Dear friends, Peter describes false teachers with a striking image: they are waterless springs and mists driven by a storm (2 Peter 2:17). They promise water and give dust.

That warning is for us too. We can look like a spring, baptised and present at every feast, and still give nothing to the thirsty who come to us. Greed is learned by practice, and so is generosity. The fast trains our hearts.

John the Baptist tells the crowds: bear fruits worthy of repentance, and do not say, we have Abraham as our ancestor (Luke 3:8). We cannot rest on our Christian heritage. When they ask, what then should we do, he says: whoever has two coats must share with anyone who has none; and whoever has food must do likewise (Luke 3:11).
Let us count our shirts and our meals this week, and share them. That is the fruit of repentance. Amen.
kids: Children, John the Baptist said: if you have two shirts, give one to someone who has none. Look in your cupboard today. Is there something you can give to a child who needs it?

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, today the forty days of the Great Fast are complete. On this Fortieth Friday, and on the feast of St Joseph, the word of God speaks of prayer, peace, life and obedience.

Abraham goes back to the place where he had pleaded with God for Sodom and sees only smoke. But Scripture says: God remembered Abraham, and sent Lot out of the midst of the overthrow (Genesis 19:29). No prayer for another person is ever wasted.

When the tribes east of the Jordan built an altar, the rest of Israel almost went to war. But they spoke first, and the misunderstanding was healed. Paul tells us: welcome one another, therefore, just as Christ has welcomed you (Romans 15:7).

At the tomb of Lazarus, Jesus says: take away the stone. Martha fears the stench of death. Jesus answers: did I not tell you that if you believed, you would see the glory of God? (John 11:40). Then he cries: Lazarus, come out! And he tells the people: unbind him, and let him go.

Christ alone gives life; through his Church he unbinds us. In these days, let us come to the sacrament of reconciliation and let the bands of sin be loosed. Lazarus points to Easter, when Christ will rise never to die again.

St Joseph never speaks in the Gospels. When the angel told him in a dream not to be afraid, he woke up and did as the angel of the Lord commanded (Matthew 1:24). As we enter the Week of the Passion, let us learn from him to obey without delay and to trust that God is with us. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus called out loud to his friend Lazarus who had died: Lazarus, come out! And he came out alive! Jesus is stronger than death.
Today we also remember St Joseph, who took care of Jesus and Mary. Let us help our fathers and mothers today, just as St Joseph helped his family.

homily: Dear friends, Paul tells the elders of Ephesus that he is going to Jerusalem as a captive to the Spirit. Prison and persecution wait for him. Yet he says: I do not count my life of any value to myself, if only I may finish my course (Acts 20:24).
He reminds them of a word of the Lord Jesus: it is more blessed to give than to receive (Acts 20:35). Then they kneel together, weep and embrace him on the shore.

Six days before the Passover, Mary of Bethany pours a pound of costly nard on Jesus' feet and wipes them with her hair. The house was filled with the fragrance of the perfume (John 12:3). Jesus says she has kept it for the day of his burial.
Tomorrow we wave palms and cry Hosanna. Tonight let us ask what we will pour out at his feet this week. Let our homes be filled with the fragrance of prayer and love. Amen.
kids: Children, Mary gave Jesus her most precious perfume, and the whole house smelled lovely. What is something special you can give to Jesus this week? Maybe your time in prayer, or a kind act for someone at home.

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, the Hosanna is over and the Hasha week has begun, the week of the Lord's suffering. The Church opens it with Joseph, the beloved son whom his father sends to his brothers: come, I will send you to them; and Joseph answers, here I am (Genesis 37:13).

His brothers see him coming and say: here comes this dreamer; come now, let us kill him (Genesis 37:19–20). The Fathers saw Christ in Joseph. The Father sends his beloved Son to us, his brothers and sisters, knowing that he will be rejected. He comes anyway. He is seeking us.

The tribes of Israel almost go to war over an altar by the Jordan, but they stop and listen, and the quarrel is healed. This week the whole parish will gather at one altar on Pesaha evening. Let no quarrel in our family or parish still be standing then.

Hebrews tells us who it is that suffers this week: the Son whom all God's angels worship, whose throne is forever and ever (Hebrews 1:6, 8). The one who is bound, mocked and crucified is the eternal Son of God.

In the council Caiaphas says it is better for one man to die for the people. John tells us that Jesus died not for the nation only, but to gather into one the dispersed children of God (John 11:52). Not one people against another, but all our sins put him on the Cross, and his love gathers us all. Let us go up with him to Jerusalem this week. Amen.
kids: Children, Joseph's father sent him to find his brothers, and Joseph said: Here I am! God the Father sent Jesus to find us. This week, when someone calls you, can you answer happily: Here I am?

homily: Dear friends, Joseph's brothers stripped him of his robe and threw him into a pit with no water in it. Then they sat down to eat (Genesis 37:24–25). And they sold their own brother for twenty pieces of silver. It all began with jealousy.

Let us be honest: jealousy still divides our families, over property, money or a parent's love. The Fathers saw Christ in Joseph: stripped of his garments, handed over for silver. But God did not abandon Joseph in the pit, and he will not abandon his Son in the tomb.

Hebrews tells us that in the days of his flesh Jesus offered prayers with loud cries and tears, and learned obedience through what he suffered (Hebrews 5:7–8). He is a high priest who knows our weakness. Let us pray today for our priests, chosen from among us, that they may be gentle with the wayward.

Some Greeks came to Philip and said: sir, we wish to see Jesus (John 12:21). Jesus answered with a grain of wheat. Unless it falls into the earth and dies, it remains just a single grain; but if it dies, it bears much fruit (John 12:24). His glory is the Cross.

Every farmer knows that seed kept in the granary feeds no one. This week, let us sow something of ourselves: a comfort given up, a jealousy uprooted, an hour given to God. On Thursday, the grain of wheat that died for us will be placed in our hands. Amen.
kids: Children, a seed has to go into the ground before it can grow into a big plant full of fruit. Jesus gave his life for us like that seed. Can you give up something today to make someone else happy?

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, Joseph is in prison, though he has done nothing wrong. He explains the dreams of Pharaoh's cupbearer and baker: a cup of wine, baskets of bread, three days. And he begs the cupbearer: remember me when it is well with you (Genesis 40:14).

But the chief cupbearer did not remember Joseph, but forgot him (Genesis 40:23). How often we are like him: we forget those who helped us, and we forget God when things go well. On Friday a dying man will say, Jesus, remember me, and Jesus will not forget.
Old Joshua tells Israel: be very careful, therefore, to love the LORD your God (Joshua 23:11). Tomorrow Jesus will give his farewell at the supper table, and his commandment too will be love.

Hebrews says that Christ has appeared once for all to remove sin by the sacrifice of himself (Hebrews 9:26). The Holy Qurbana does not repeat that sacrifice; it makes the one sacrifice of the Cross present for us. Let us come to it tomorrow with clean hearts.

In the Gospel Jesus says: now my soul is troubled. But he does not run from the hour: Father, glorify your name. And I, when I am lifted up from the earth, will draw all people to myself (John 12:32). Tonight, as we prepare the Pesaha appam, let us look at the Cross and let him draw us. Amen.
kids: Children, Joseph asked a man in prison: please remember me! But the man forgot. Jesus never forgets us! Tonight, can you help prepare the Pesaha appam, and say thank you to someone you forgot to thank?

homily: Dear friends, in the early Church this week belonged to the newly baptised. They came to church every day in their white garments to understand the new life they had received. Today the readings speak to them, and to all of us who were baptised.

Isaiah promised a city that had been abandoned: “The LORD will be your everlasting light, and your days of mourning shall be ended.” On Easter morning the days of mourning ended. Christ is our light that never sets.

Peter preached: David died and his tomb is still with us; but “this Jesus God raised up, and of that all of us are witnesses.” The empty tomb beside the full tomb: that is the whole difference. Jesus is alive, and he has poured out the Holy Spirit.

Paul tells us how we receive this life: by faith, like Abraham, who “believed God, and it was reckoned to him as righteousness.” And he sings with David: “Blessed are those whose iniquities are forgiven.” Our sins were washed away in Baptism, not because we earned it, but as a gift.

Jesus promised: “I will not leave you orphaned; I am coming to you… because I live, you also will live.” He promised that the Father and he would make their home in us, and that the Holy Spirit would teach us. And he gave us his peace, not as the world gives.
This week, let us carry his peace home. Each evening, say to one another: The peace of the Lord be with you. Because he lives, we live. Alleluia! Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus promised his friends: ‘I will not leave you alone.’ And he kept his promise: he rose from the dead, and he is always with us!
Jesus gives us his peace, a quiet, happy feeling inside. Tonight, say to your family: ‘The peace of Jesus be with you!’

homily: Dear friends, Isaiah's words were read by Jesus in Nazareth: “The spirit of the Lord GOD is upon me… to proclaim liberty to the captives.” At Easter he has freed the greatest prisoners of all, the prisoners of death. He gives “a garland instead of ashes, the oil of gladness instead of mourning.” The ashes of the Great Fast have become the garland of Easter.

When Peter preached, the people were cut to the heart and asked: “Brothers, what should we do?” He told them: repent and be baptised. Three thousand were baptised that day. And they devoted themselves to four things: the apostles' teaching, fellowship, the breaking of bread and the prayers. These are still the four pillars of every family and every parish.
Paul says plainly: if Christ has not been raised, our faith is futile. Our faith is not a beautiful story. It rests on a fact: Jesus rose from the dead in his body, and we too will rise.

Then the road to Emmaus. Two disciples walk away from Jerusalem, sad. “But we had hoped,” they say. How many of us have said those words? And Jesus walks beside them, unrecognised. He opens the Scriptures, beginning with Moses and all the prophets, and their hearts begin to burn.

At the table he breaks the bread, and they know him. That is the shape of every Qurbana: first the Word, then the Bread, then the road back to tell the others. Jesus does not wait for us to be happy before he walks with us. He comes to us when we are sad.

This week, let us walk with someone who is sad, as Jesus did. Let us read the Scriptures and ask him to explain them. And at every Qurbana, let us recognise him in the breaking of the bread. Alleluia! Amen.
kids: Children, two friends of Jesus were walking home very sad. Jesus walked with them, but they did not know him until he broke the bread!
Jesus is with us too, even when we cannot see him. At Holy Qurbana, when the priest breaks the Bread, let us say in our hearts: ‘It is you, Jesus!’

homily: Dear friends, Isaiah sings: “I will greatly rejoice in the LORD… for he has clothed me with the garments of salvation.” The newly baptised wore white this week. All of us were clothed with Christ in Baptism. And God speaks to his people as a bridegroom: “You shall no more be termed Forsaken… but you shall be called My Delight Is in Her.” Each of us can hear the Risen Lord say: you are my delight.

In Acts, Peter and John are threatened for preaching Jesus. The community gathers and prays. They do not ask God to remove the threats; they ask for boldness: “grant to your servants to speak your word with all boldness.” And the place is shaken, and they are filled with the Holy Spirit.

Paul writes from prison: lead a life worthy of your calling, “with all humility and gentleness, with patience, bearing with one another in love.” There is one body, one Spirit, one Lord, one faith, one baptism, one God and Father of all. A Church that prays together and stays one cannot be defeated.

And Jesus says: “I am the vine, you are the branches… apart from me you can do nothing.” A branch does not bear fruit by trying harder, but by staying attached. We stay attached to him through prayer, through his word, through keeping his commandments, and above all through the Holy Qurbana: “Those who eat my flesh and drink my blood abide in me, and I in them.”
Sometimes the Father prunes us. It hurts. But he cuts only to make us bear more fruit. Many of us can look back and see that a hard time was a fruitful time.

This week, let us abide. Ten minutes before the Blessed Sacrament, or ten minutes with the Gospel. Let us ask for boldness to speak of Jesus, and bear patiently with one difficult person. Apart from him we can do nothing; with him we bear much fruit. Alleluia! Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus said: ‘I am the vine, you are the branches.’ A branch stays green and grows fruit only when it is joined to the plant.
We stay joined to Jesus when we pray, go to Holy Qurbana and love others. Let us stay close to Jesus every day!

intro: Theme: “Let anyone who is thirsty come to me, and let the one who believes in me drink.”
Hagar and the God who sees, an oath kept and strangers brought to the altar, the living sacrifice, and Christ the living water and the light of the world.

sub: A runaway slave in the desert.
Where have you come from, where are you going?
q: So she named the LORD who spoke to her, “You are El-roi”; for she said, “Have I really seen God and remained alive after seeing him?”
But whenever you pray, go into your room and shut the door and pray to your Father who is in secret; and your Father who sees in secret will reward you.
points.apply: Notice one person who serves you unseen; thank them by name and pay them justly.

points.h: Wood and water for the altar
sub: A treaty obtained by a trick.
An oath kept even to one's hurt.
q: But on that day Joshua made them hewers of wood and drawers of water for the congregation and for the altar of the LORD, to continue to this day, in the place that he should choose.
For the Son of Man came not to be served but to serve, and to give his life a ransom for many.”
points.apply: Keep one promise you have delayed, and offer one humble service in your parish.

q: The sacrifice acceptable to God is a broken spirit; a broken and contrite heart, O God, you will not despise.
I appeal to you therefore, brothers and sisters, by the mercies of God, to present your bodies as a living sacrifice, holy and acceptable to God, which is your spiritual worship.
points.apply: Choose one discipline of eyes, tongue or hands and offer it each morning this week.

points.h: Living water and the light of the world
q: With joy you will draw water from the wells of salvation.
Again Jesus spoke to them, saying, “I am the light of the world. Whoever follows me will never walk in darkness but will have the light of life.”
points.apply: Light a candle at home on the anniversary of your Baptism, or this Sunday evening, and renew your baptismal promises as a family.

concl: The God who saw Hagar sees us; the God who brought the Gibeonites to his altar brings us near; the Son pours out the Spirit like rivers and shines as the light of the world.
Let us see the unseen, keep our word, offer our bodies, and come thirsty to Christ.
2027-03-07.resolve: This week, thank one unseen servant by name, keep one delayed promise, and renew your baptismal promises with a lit candle.

intro: Theme: “I am the good shepherd. The good shepherd lays down his life for the sheep.”
Lot who lingered and was taken by the hand, the promises that never failed, the brother for whom Christ died, and the Shepherd who lays down his life of his own accord.

q: But he lingered; so the men seized him and his wife and his two daughters by the hand, the LORD being merciful to him, and they brought him out and left him outside the city.
points.apply: Make a definite break before Hosanna Sunday with the one thing you keep looking back at.

q: Not one of all the good promises that the LORD had made to the house of Israel had failed; all came to pass.
For in him every one of God's promises is a “Yes.” For this reason it is through him that we say the “Amen,” to the glory of God.
points.apply: Write down three promises God has kept in your life, and thank him for them at the family prayer.

sub: The strong and the weak in Rome.
The one for whom Christ died.
q: You shall not revile the deaf or put a stumbling block before the blind; you shall fear your God: I am the LORD.
For the kingdom of God is not food and drink but righteousness and peace and joy in the Holy Spirit.
points.apply: Give up for the rest of the fast one thing that might make someone close to you stumble.

q: I myself will be the shepherd of my sheep, and I will make them lie down, says the Lord GOD.
I am the good shepherd. The good shepherd lays down his life for the sheep.
points.apply: Pray each day this week for your bishop, your parish priest, and vocations from your parish.

concl: God's mercy takes us by the hand when we linger, and every one of his promises is Yes in Christ.
Let us never be a stumbling block, and let us follow the Good Shepherd who goes freely to Jerusalem to lay down his life for us.
2027-03-14.resolve: This week, break with what you keep looking back at, remove one stumbling block, and pray daily for your shepherds.

intro: Theme: “Hosanna to the Son of David! Blessed is the one who comes in the name of the Lord! Hosanna in the highest heaven!”
Hosanna Sunday: the King from Judah, the humble King of peace, the cleansing of the house of prayer, and the branches grafted onto a holy root.

sub: The colt bound to the vine.
The Lion of Judah who conquers by the Cross.
q: The scepter shall not depart from Judah, nor the ruler’s staff from between his feet, until tribute comes to him; and the obedience of the peoples is his.
Then one of the elders said to me, “Do not weep. See, the Lion of the tribe of Judah, the Root of David, has conquered, so that he can open the scroll and its seven seals.”
points.apply: Give Christ the throne of one area of your life you have kept for yourself.

points.h: Humble and riding on a donkey
q: Rejoice greatly, O daughter Zion! Shout aloud, O daughter Jerusalem! Lo, your king comes to you; triumphant and victorious is he, humble and riding on a donkey, on a colt, the foal of a donkey.
The crowds that went ahead of him and that followed were shouting, “Hosanna to the Son of David! Blessed is the one who comes in the name of the Lord! Hosanna in the highest heaven!”
points.apply: Choose gentleness over force in one conflict at home or at work this week.

sub: The blind and the lame healed.
q: these I will bring to my holy mountain, and make them joyful in my house of prayer; their burnt offerings and their sacrifices will be accepted on my altar; for my house shall be called a house of prayer for all peoples.
He said to them, “It is written, ‘My house shall be called a house of prayer’; but you are making it a den of robbers.”
points.apply: Gather your family for prayer every evening this week, and let the house be quieter.

sub: Do not boast over the branches.
q: But I am like a green olive tree in the house of God. I trust in the steadfast love of God forever and ever.
do not boast over the branches. If you do boast, remember that it is not you that support the root, but the root that supports you.
points.apply: Refuse every word of contempt this week, and pray for the Jewish people and for all Christians.

concl: The King promised to Judah comes humble on a donkey, cleanses the house of prayer and heals; the children greet him with Hosanna.
We are branches grafted by grace; let our Hosanna last through the whole week, to the Cross and the empty tomb.
2027-03-21.resolve: Keep the blessed palm, pray with your family every evening, and follow the Lord through every service of the Week of the Passion.

intro: Theme: “Having loved his own who were in the world, he loved them to the end.”
The Passover lamb, Malachi's pure offering, the Body and Blood of the Lord given on the night he was betrayed, and the Lord who kneels to wash our feet.

q: The blood shall be a sign for you on the houses where you live: when I see the blood, I will pass over you, and no plague shall destroy you when I strike the land of Egypt.
Clean out the old yeast so that you may be a new batch, as you really are unleavened. For our paschal lamb, Christ, has been sacrificed.
points.apply: Keep the home Pesaha tonight, and pray that the blood of the Lamb may protect your family.

points.h: A pure offering in every place
sub: From the rising of the sun to its setting.
q: For from the rising of the sun to its setting my name is great among the nations, and in every place incense is offered to my name, and a pure offering; for my name is great among the nations, says the LORD of hosts.
For as often as you eat this bread and drink the cup, you proclaim the Lord's death until he comes.
points.apply: Give the Lord your best tonight: come early, prepared and reconciled.

sub: On the night he was betrayed.
Do this in remembrance of me.
q: The days are surely coming, says the LORD, when I will make a new covenant with the house of Israel and the house of Judah.
for this is my blood of the covenant, which is poured out for many for the forgiveness of sins.
points.apply: Receive Communion tonight with a clean heart, and pray for the priests who make the Lord present for you.

q: Let a little water be brought, and wash your feet, and rest yourselves under the tree.
So if I, your Lord and Teacher, have washed your feet, you also ought to wash one another's feet.
points.apply: Do one humble service at home tonight, and watch one hour with the Lord.

concl: The Lamb of God gives us his Body and Blood, and the Lord of all kneels at our feet: the altar and the basin belong together.
Having loved his own, he loved them to the end; let us receive him worthily, serve one another, and watch with him tonight.
2027-03-25.resolve: Come to the one Qurbana, keep the home Pesaha, do one humble service, and watch one hour.

intro: Theme: “When Jesus had received the wine, he said, ‘It is finished.’ Then he bowed his head and gave up his spirit.”
The lamb that God provides, the Servant wounded for us, the words from the Cross, and the Church born from the pierced side.

points.h: God himself will provide the lamb
sub: Your son, your only son, whom you love.
On Calvary no hand is stopped.
q: Abraham said, “God himself will provide the lamb for a burnt offering, my son.” So the two of them walked on together.
For God so loved the world that he gave his only Son, so that everyone who believes in him may not perish but may have eternal life.
points.apply: Look at a crucifix for five minutes today and say only: you were given for me.

points.h: By his bruises we are healed
sub: The sins of all laid on one.
q: But he was wounded for our transgressions, crushed for our iniquities; upon him was the punishment that made us whole, and by his bruises we are healed.
But God proves his love for us in that while we still were sinners Christ died for us.
points.apply: Bring one hidden sin to the Cross today, and plan to confess it in Easter week.

sub: No one is to blame but sin.
q: All we like sheep have gone astray; we have all turned to our own way, and the LORD has laid on him the iniquity of us all.
Then Jesus said, “Father, forgive them; for they do not know what they are doing.”
points.apply: Forgive one person by name today, and if possible tell them.

sub: The Church born from the new Adam.
q: They gave me poison for food, and for my thirst they gave me vinegar to drink.
Instead, one of the soldiers pierced his side with a spear, and at once blood and water came out.
points.apply: Take the kaippuneer today as a promise not to run from your own cross.

concl: What Abraham was spared, God gave; what we deserved, Christ bore; what was torn open on the Cross is the door of the Church.
Kneel, kiss the wounds, forgive, and stand with Mary until the morning comes.
2027-03-26.resolve: Today keep the fast with love, venerate the Cross with your family, forgive one person by name, and keep the evening in silence.

intro: Theme: “Therefore we have been buried with him by baptism into death, so that, just as Christ was raised from the dead by the glory of the Father, so we too might walk in newness of life.”
The great silence of the tomb, the sign of Jonah, our burial and rising in Baptism, and the stone rolled away.

sub: He goes down among the dead.
q: Abraham called that place “The LORD will provide”; as it is said to this day, “On the mount of the LORD it shall be provided.”
For Christ also suffered for sins once for all, the righteous for the unrighteous, in order to bring you to God. He was put to death in the flesh, but made alive in the spirit,
points.apply: Keep one hour of today in silence, waiting with Mary.

q: I called to the LORD out of my distress, and he answered me; out of the belly of Sheol I cried, and you heard my voice.
For just as Jonah was three days and three nights in the belly of the sea monster, so for three days and three nights the Son of Man will be in the heart of the earth.
points.apply: Bring to God the place in your life that feels like the bottom of the sea.

q: I will sprinkle clean water upon you, and you shall be clean from all your uncleannesses, and from all your idols I will cleanse you.
Do you not know that all of us who have been baptized into Christ Jesus were baptized into his death?
points.apply: Renew your baptismal promises today with full attention, and find your baptism date.

q: Then the LORD spoke to the fish, and it spewed Jonah out upon the dry land.
He is not here; for he has been raised, as he said. Come, see the place where he lay.
points.apply: Bring the whole family to the Resurrection service tonight.

concl: The silence of Saturday is the silence before the shout: the Lord who went down among the dead is about to rise.
Bury the old self with him, renew your promises, and come to the Uyirppu with your lamp lit.
2027-03-27.resolve: Today, keep part of the day in silence, renew your baptismal promises, find your baptism date, and bring your family to the Uyirppu.

intro: Theme: “He is not here; for he has been raised, as he said. Come, see the place where he lay.”
The light risen over Jerusalem, Hannah's song of reversals, our new life in Christ, and the Lord who calls us by name.

sub: The glory of the LORD has risen.
q: Arise, shine; for your light has come, and the glory of the LORD has risen upon you.
Again Jesus spoke to them, saying, “I am the light of the world. Whoever follows me will never walk in darkness but will have the light of life.”
points.apply: Let your Easter joy be visible today: greet, visit, share.

points.h: He raises up from the dust
sub: The LORD kills and brings to life.
q: The LORD kills and brings to life; he brings down to Sheol and raises up.
But in fact Christ has been raised from the dead, the first fruits of those who have died.
points.apply: Thank God today for one place where he has lifted you from the dust.

points.h: Dead to sin, alive to God
q: This is the day that the LORD has made; let us rejoice and be glad in it.
So you also must consider yourselves dead to sin and alive to God in Christ Jesus.
points.apply: Leave one sin in the tomb this Easter and plan a good confession this week.

q: But now thus says the LORD, he who created you, O Jacob, he who formed you, O Israel: Do not fear, for I have redeemed you; I have called you by name, you are mine.
Jesus said to her, “Mary!” She turned and said to him in Hebrew, “Rabbouni!” (which means Teacher).
points.apply: Tell one person today, in your own words, why you believe Jesus is alive.

concl: The tomb is empty, the light has come, and the Lord who was crucified calls us by name.
Live as people raised from the dead, and go and tell: I have seen the Lord.
2027-03-28.resolve: This Easter, greet everyone with ‘Christ is risen’, share your table with someone alone, and pray the Queen of Heaven daily until Pentecost.

intro: Theme: “Do you want to be made well?”
Abram's journey with an altar, Achan's confession, Paul's love for his people, and the man by the pool who was told to stand up and walk.

sub: A call with a blank map.
q: Now the LORD said to Abram, “Go from your country and your kindred and your father's house to the land that I will show you.
By faith Abraham obeyed when he was called to set out for a place that he was to receive as an inheritance; and he set out, not knowing where he was going.
points.apply: Set apart one place and one fixed time for prayer wherever you are this week.

sub: Do not hide it from me.
The valley of trouble becomes a door of hope.
q: Then Joshua said to Achan, “My son, give glory to the LORD God of Israel and make confession to him. Tell me now what you have done; do not hide it from me.”
Therefore confess your sins to one another, and pray for one another, so that you may be healed.
points.apply: Make a careful examination of conscience and go to confession before Palm Sunday.

points.h: Stand up, take your mat and walk
q: then the lame shall leap like a deer, and the tongue of the speechless sing for joy. For waters shall break forth in the wilderness, and streams in the desert;
Jesus said to him, “Stand up, take your mat and walk.”
points.apply: Name the excuse you give most often, and replace it this week with one act of obedience.

concl: God calls us to go, to confess, and to stand up.
Abram went, Achan confessed, the sick man walked: halfway through the fast, it is our turn.
2027-03-01.resolve: This week, answer Jesus' question with a confession and one concrete step.

intro: Theme: “So it depends not on human will or exertion, but on God who shows mercy.”
Abram's fear in Egypt, Israel sent back to Ai, the mercy of God, and the Son who does what the Father does.

sub: God protects the one who is sacrificed.
q: Say you are my sister, so that it may go well with me because of you, and that my life may be spared on your account.
So then, putting away falsehood, let all of us speak the truth to our neighbors, for we are members of one another.
points.apply: Correct one half-truth this week, especially one that has hurt someone close to you.

sub: Back to the weak place, with God.
q: Then the LORD said to Joshua, “Do not fear or be dismayed; take all the fighting men with you, and go up now to Ai.
Peace I leave with you; my peace I give to you. I do not give to you as the world gives. Do not let your hearts be troubled, and do not let them be afraid.
points.apply: Name the place where you usually fall, and plan one change there with prayer.

sub: Is there injustice with God? By no means.
The Son does what the Father does.
q: I will be gracious to whom I will be gracious, and will show mercy on whom I will show mercy.
So it depends not on human will or exertion, but on God who shows mercy.
points.apply: Offer your fast today not as a payment but as thanksgiving for mercy received.

concl: Our heroes stumble, our battles are lost and won again, and everything rests on mercy.
The Son shows us the Father's face: honour him, and do what you see him doing.
2027-03-02.resolve: This week, tell the truth where fear has made you hide it, and thank God each night for one mercy received.

intro: Theme: “Lord, to whom can we go? You have the words of eternal life.”
Mid-Lent: Abram's generosity, the outstretched hand that points to the Cross, the word of faith on our lips, and Peter's answer.

sub: The elder lets the younger choose.
The one who lets go receives everything.
q: Then Abram said to Lot, “Let there be no strife between you and me, and between your herders and my herders; for we are kindred.
If it is possible, so far as it depends on you, live peaceably with all.
points.apply: Take one step toward peace in a family quarrel over property or inheritance before Palm Sunday.

sub: Confess with your lips, believe in your heart.
q: No, the word is very near to you; it is in your mouth and in your heart for you to observe.
because if you confess with your lips that Jesus is Lord and believe in your heart that God raised him from the dead, you will be saved.
points.apply: Say aloud each morning this week: Jesus is Lord, and God raised him from the dead.

sub: Peter's answer for the whole Church.
q: You show me the path of life. In your presence there is fullness of joy; in your right hand are pleasures forevermore.
Simon Peter answered him, “Lord, to whom can we go? You have the words of eternal life.
points.apply: Take up again one Lenten resolution you dropped, and make a visit to the Blessed Sacrament this week.

concl: At the middle of the fast, the Cross is held up and the question is asked again: do you also wish to go away?
Let go for the sake of peace, confess Jesus as Lord, and stay with the one who has the words of eternal life.
2027-03-03.resolve: Today, renew your fast and take one step toward peace.

intro: Theme: “God has not rejected his people whom he foreknew.”
Abram goes after Lot, Joshua gathers all the people around the word and the altar, God keeps a remnant by grace, and Jesus waits for the Father's hour.

sub: Abram did not say: it is his fault.
Love that goes after the one who strayed.
q: When Abram heard that his nephew had been taken captive, he led forth his trained men, born in his house, three hundred eighteen of them, and went in pursuit as far as Dan.
“Which one of you, having a hundred sheep and losing one of them, does not leave the ninety-nine in the wilderness and go after the one that is lost until he finds it?
points.apply: Contact one person who has drifted away, simply to show that you care.

q: There was not a word of all that Moses commanded that Joshua did not read before all the assembly of Israel, and the women, and the little ones, and the aliens who resided among them.
Then he began to say to them, “Today this scripture has been fulfilled in your hearing.”
points.apply: After this week's Holy Qurbana, ask each child at home what they heard in the readings.

sub: God has not rejected his people.
Jesus waits for the Father's hour.
q: Yet I will leave seven thousand in Israel, all the knees that have not bowed to Baal, and every mouth that has not kissed him.”
So too at the present time there is a remnant, chosen by grace.
points.apply: Do one good work this week in secret, and do not mention it to anyone.

concl: God goes after the lost, gathers all his people, and never takes back his call.
Let us go after those who have strayed, make room for everyone at the word and the altar, and trust the Father's hour.
2027-03-04.resolve: This week, reach out to one person who has drifted away, and bring the children to the word and the altar.

intro: Theme: “And he believed the LORD; and the LORD reckoned it to him as righteousness.”
First Friday: the stars and the covenant between the pieces, the mouldy bread of Gibeon, the depth of God's riches, and the pierced Heart of the one the Father sent.

q: And he believed the LORD; and the LORD reckoned it to him as righteousness.
No distrust made him waver concerning the promise of God, but he grew strong in his faith as he gave glory to God, being fully convinced that God was able to do what he had promised.
points.apply: Name one promise of God you find hard to believe, and pray with it each night this week.

points.h: They did not ask the Lord
q: Trust in the LORD with all your heart, and do not rely on your own insight. In all your ways acknowledge him, and he will make straight your paths.
If any of you is lacking in wisdom, ask God, who gives to all generously and ungrudgingly, and it will be given you.
points.apply: Bring one decision before the Blessed Sacrament before you act on it.

q: For my thoughts are not your thoughts, nor are your ways my ways, says the LORD. For as the heavens are higher than the earth, so are my ways higher than your ways and my thoughts than your thoughts.
O the depth of the riches and wisdom and knowledge of God! How unsearchable are his judgments and how inscrutable his ways!
points.apply: End each day this week with a few minutes of simple praise, asking nothing.

sub: His hour had not yet come.
q: And I will pour out a spirit of compassion and supplication on the house of David and the inhabitants of Jerusalem, so that, when they look on the one whom they have pierced, they shall mourn for him, as one mourns for an only child, and weep bitterly over him, as one weeps over a firstborn.
Instead, one of the soldiers pierced his side with a spear, and at once blood and water came out.
points.apply: Renew the consecration of your family to the Sacred Heart today.

concl: God binds himself to us with a covenant he keeps alone, all the way to the pierced Heart on the Cross.
Believe like Abram, ask before you decide, praise the depth of his riches, and rest in the Heart that was opened for you.
2027-03-05.resolve: Keep this First Friday with confession, Holy Qurbana and the consecration of your family to the Sacred Heart.

intro: Theme: “Never has anyone spoken like this!”
The Christian as citizen under God, the guards who only listened, and Nicodemus who asked for a fair hearing.

q: By me kings reign, and rulers decree what is just;
Let every person be subject to the governing authorities; for there is no authority except from God, and those authorities that exist have been instituted by God.
points.apply: Make sure your taxes, bills and documents are honest, and refuse every bribe.

points.h: Never has anyone spoken like this
q: I will raise up for them a prophet like you from among their own people; I will put my words in the mouth of the prophet, who shall speak to them everything that I command.
The police answered, “Never has anyone spoken like this!”
points.apply: Read the Passion according to John slowly before Palm Sunday, as if hearing it for the first time.

q: You must not be partial in judging: hear out the small and the great alike; you shall not be intimidated by anyone, for the judgment is God's. Any case that is too hard for you, bring to me, and I will hear it.”
“Our law does not judge people without first giving them a hearing to find out what they are doing, does it?”
points.apply: When someone is criticised in their absence, ask that their side be heard first.

concl: A Christian is an honest citizen, a careful listener and a fair judge, faithful to God above all.
Listen to the One whose word is like no other, and find the courage of Nicodemus.
2027-03-06.resolve: This week, be honest in every duty, and defend one person who is being judged without a hearing.

intro: Theme: “There is still one thing lacking. Sell all that you own and distribute the money to the poor, and you will have treasure in heaven; then come, follow me.”
The shadow and the substance, the good man who stopped one step short, and the call to follow Jesus with an undivided heart.

q: Is not this the fast that I choose: to loose the bonds of injustice, to undo the thongs of the yoke, to let the oppressed go free, and to break every yoke?
These are only a shadow of what is to come, but the substance belongs to Christ.
points.apply: Let your fast today end in one act of justice or kindness to someone who is burdened.

sub: A good man with a sincere question.
A Person, not one more rule.
q: Put no confidence in extortion, and set no vain hopes on robbery; if riches increase, do not set your heart on them.
There is still one thing lacking. Sell all that you own and distribute the money to the poor, and you will have treasure in heaven; then come, follow me.
points.apply: Ask the Lord in silence today: what is the one thing still lacking in me? Write down the answer.

q: Whoever is kind to the poor lends to the LORD, and will be repaid in full.
For where your treasure is, there your heart will be also.
points.apply: Give this week, to the Lenten box or to a person in need, what your fasting has saved.

concl: Every fast is a shadow; Christ is the substance, and he asks for the heart, not only the plate.
The ruler kept the commandments and went away sad; let us give, and come, and follow.
2027-03-08.resolve: Give away this week what the fast has saved, and do not judge anyone else's fast.

intro: Theme: “Go and do likewise.”
God who gives seed to the sower, the Samaritan who was moved with pity, and the indescribable gift that turns all our giving into thanksgiving.

q: Since there will never cease to be some in need on the earth, I therefore command you, “Open your hand to the poor and needy neighbor in your land.”
He who supplies seed to the sower and bread for food will supply and multiply your seed for sowing and increase the harvest of your righteousness.
points.apply: Fix a definite Lenten alms today and give it before Hosanna Sunday.

sub: The priest and the Levite passed by.
Oil, wine, an inn and two denarii.
q: He has told you, O mortal, what is good; and what does the LORD require of you but to do justice, and to love kindness, and to walk humbly with your God?
But a Samaritan while traveling came near him; and when he saw him, he was moved with pity.
points.apply: Come near this week to one person you have been passing by.

q: What shall I return to the LORD for all his bounty to me?
Thanks be to God for his indescribable gift!
points.apply: Before Communion at your next Qurbana, thank Christ by name for one wound he has healed in you.

concl: Almsgiving is sowing in God's field, and its harvest is thanksgiving and communion.
Christ came near to us on our road; let us go and do likewise.
2027-03-09.resolve: Choose one person you have been passing by, and come near to them before Sunday.

intro: Theme: “Neither do I condemn you. Go your way, and from now on do not sin again.”
The waterless clouds of Jude, the archangel who left judgment to God, and the meeting of misery and mercy in the temple.

sub: Trees that bear fruit in season.
q: They are like trees planted by streams of water, which yield their fruit in its season, and their leaves do not wither. In all that they do, they prosper.
They are waterless clouds carried along by the winds; autumn trees without fruit, twice dead, uprooted;
points.apply: Name one promise you made to God or to someone else this Lent, and keep it today.

sub: Michael did not dare to slander.
q: And the LORD said to Satan, “The LORD rebuke you, O Satan! The LORD who has chosen Jerusalem rebuke you! Is not this man a brand plucked from the fire?”
When they kept on questioning him, he straightened up and said to them, “Let anyone among you who is without sin be the first to throw a stone at her.”
points.apply: For one day, say nothing negative about anyone who is not present.

sub: Go, and do not sin again.
q: As I live, says the Lord GOD, I have no pleasure in the death of the wicked, but that the wicked turn from their ways and live;
Neither do I condemn you. Go your way, and from now on do not sin again.
points.apply: Make your Lenten confession this week, and choose one concrete step away from your most frequent sin.

concl: Judgment belongs to God, who does not want the death of the sinner but his life.
Let us put down our stones, receive his mercy, and go out to sin no more.
2027-03-10.resolve: Go to confession before Hosanna Sunday, and pray each day this week for one person you have judged.

intro: Theme: “for, while physical training is of some value, godliness is valuable in every way, holding promise for both the present life and the life to come.”
The training of godliness, the road up to Jerusalem, and the eyes that cannot yet see the meaning of the Cross.

q: He humbled you by letting you hunger, then by feeding you with manna, with which neither you nor your ancestors were acquainted, in order to make you understand that one does not live by bread alone, but by every word that comes from the mouth of the LORD.
for, while physical training is of some value, godliness is valuable in every way, holding promise for both the present life and the life to come.
points.apply: Choose one spiritual exercise and practise it every day until Easter without fail.

sub: On the third day he will rise.
